a31a2b2d345a03a1: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expand its Whitening The Black Spot initiative nationwide in stages, beginning with Penang, said Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.

“We are doing it contingent by contingent through engagements and town halls in each district. We will work with all agencies, the community, NGOs and local leadership to resolve issues,” he told reporters after the initiative’s Penang Contingent launch at the PICCA@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre.

Also present were Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin, Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng and Mohd Khalid’s wife Puan Sri Munirah Che Rose.
Mohd Khalid said the Penang phase will run for a month before being expanded to black spots in other states battling high crime rates or pressing security issues.

He emphasised that the initiative is a comprehensive preventive approach covering patrols, focused operations, CCTV system improvements, gotong-royong, community programmes, safety education and social intervention.
He added that 41 departments and agencies have been mobilised through an integrated Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach to create a safer environment in Penang.

“It emphasises the principles of Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED), such as lighting, cleanliness, maintenance, environmental design and public facilities, to close off spaces and opportunities for crime,” he said.
Mohd Khalid said the pilot locations are Bukit Jambul, Sungai Nibong, Kampung Ujong Batu, Permatang Pauh, Sungai Rambai, Pondok Upeh and Bukit Panchor.

“We need to see whether crime rates drop, whether the areas become more orderly, whether the police presence is increasingly felt and whether the community truly feels safer. Real success is change that can be seen, felt and believed in by the whole community,” he said.
Meanwhile, Lim said Whitening the Blackspot will target areas deemed unsafe, high-risk and uncomfortable, such as dark, dirty spots, abandoned buildings and poorly maintained recreational areas.
He said the three main goals are to transform blackspots into safer spaces, cut crime opportunities in hotspots, and build more harmonious, safe neighbourhoods.

“For example, an abandoned village building may have become a haunt for drug addicts, or a park may have unkempt play areas with no lighting, broken benches and dark, dirty spots. We want to turn these into clean, well-lit spaces the community can use safely,” he said.

Lim said district police chiefs across five Penang districts have proposed 38 programmes under the initiative: six in Northeast Penang, eight in Southwest Penang, six in North Seberang Perai, 13 in Central Seberang Perai and five in South Seberang Perai.

The four objectives to be met within a month are improving crime prevention, strengthening cross-agency cooperation, transforming high-risk areas into safe spaces, and empowering community involvement.

“PDRM cannot succeed alone. To make this project work, we need local communities, federal and state agencies, elected representatives, local authorities, the private sector and NGOs. Everyone must play their part, because safety is a shared responsibility,” he said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PDRM is the Malay abbreviation for Polis Diraja Malaysia.
3152a1c04881be12: LONDON: British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and the army was examining a number of vehicles after security was stepped up at a British air base used by US air forces in southwest England.

A Reuters eyewitness said armed police were blocking access to the main gate of the base. Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the village of Fairford near the base.
"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.
It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act," Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the air base.
"The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles."
A spokesperson for the US Air Force said they would not discuss specific force protection measures.

"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."

0026bbbe86489590: LOURDES, Sept 27 — Pope Leo XIV will meet today with victims of clerical sex abuse, a day after holding an open-air mass for hundreds of thousands of worshippers and praying at a holy shrine in Lourdes during his official visit to France.
The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is on a four-day trip to France, a secular country with deep Catholic roots, marking the first official papal visit there in nearly two decades.
He is expected to meet privately with seven victims after promising to further efforts to reform the Church in the wake of the global sexual abuse scandal.
A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as minors in France over the span of 70 years.

Among the victims who will meet the pope is a former pupil of the Notre-Dame de Betharram institution, a boarding school in southwestern France at the centre of widespread accusations of physical and sexual abuse over decades.

Today’s meeting comes a day after the US pontiff visited the southwestern pilgrimage town of Lourdes and prayed at the Grotto of Massabielle, where Catholic tradition holds that the Virgin Mary appeared in 1858 to a peasant girl, later canonised as Saint Bernadette.

Months ahead of a presidential election with the far-right surging and immigration high on the agenda, he prayed to the Virgin Mary to “obtain for France wise and generous leaders... eager to serve the common good”.
“May they make her (France’s) voice heard in promoting the defence of fundamental human rights and peace in the world, rejecting the mentality of war once and for all.”
AFP reporters saw him perform the rituals observed by the many pilgrims to the cave: touching the rock, lighting a candle and drinking spring water.
Giant Paris mass

In an earlier highlight of the visit’s second day, the 71-year-old pope led enthusiastic worshippers in a mass at Paris’s Place de la Concorde, where a giant white canopy was erected to serve as a makeshift altar.
His prayers were accompanied by choral and organ music as the sun broke through the grey skies.
“It is truly good and pleasant when brothers and sisters come together and glorify the greatness of God,” said Pope Leo, dressed in white liturgical vestments.
Around 800,000 people had gathered all the way beyond the Arc de Triomphe, the Vatican said.
“It’s one time in history to see the pope,” said Aline Riziki, 41, who was born in the Democratic Republic of Congo and has lived in France for 11 years.
“I dropped everything to come here and see him, to pray for peace in the east” of her homeland, racked by conflict for decades, she said.
‘Important moment’
Jeanne de Montagnac, 29, came with her husband and two-year-old girl, who was perched on his shoulders.
“We’re happy that, even if she won’t remember it, we’re sharing this with her,” she said, a small golden cross dangling over her jumper.
“It’s an important moment for us to be surrounded by other people who also have faith.”
The first US pontiff was visiting France seven months before voters choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron.
A number of presidential hopefuls were present, including far-right leader Marine Le Pen and centrist Edouard Philippe.

Macron did not attend the mass but was represented by his wife Brigitte. The president said in a message on X that France was “proud to welcome Pope Leo XIV and this monumental mass in the heart of Paris”.
‘Dignity and peace’
The pope met migrants at Maison Bakhita, an association supporting refugees, earlier on yesterday. Leo said it was “possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace”.
He also stressed the “fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love”.
The association said the pope’s visit sent a “message” ahead of the April-May election.
Leo was the third pope to visit Lourdes after Benedict XVI in 2008 and Jean-Paul II in 1983 and 2004.
The sanctuary, one of the most important Catholic holy sites in the world, receives some three million pilgrims each year. Catholics credit it with miraculous healings. — AFP
68f29a00c13665f9: SEGAMAT, Sept 27 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has re-exported 436 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin this year, with another 578 containers due to be sent out from October.
The agency said the operations were carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), Royal Malaysia Police, Department of Environment, and port authorities.
“Another 578 containers are scheduled to be sent out in stages beginning this October,” it said in a statement today.
AKPS is targeting the re-export of all 1,259 e-waste containers from Malaysia by the end of 2026.
Meanwhile, AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the agency had recorded seizures worth RM265.89 million this year, about three times the value recorded in 2025.
He said e-waste and drugs were among the main contributors to the total value of seizures and leakages intercepted by the agency.

He was speaking at a press conference after the closing ceremony of the AKPS Basic Training Course for Pioneer Officers Series 1/2026, which was also attended by Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar at the Segamat Police Training Centre here today.
On drug smuggling trends, Mohd Shuhaily said tighter controls and targeted screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport had helped curb repeated attempts to smuggle drugs.
“Enforcement at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 sees almost daily arrests involving attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers, mostly masterminded by foreigners,” he said.

The 408 pioneer AKPS officers who completed their training comprise 39 Grade KS5 Assistant Border Superintendents and 369 Grade KS1 Assistant Border Superintendents, and will begin field training at the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link entry point from Oct 1.

On plans to fill 13,721 AKPS positions at 122 entry points nationwide, Mohd Shuhaily said recruitment was being carried out in stages through service scheme offers to personnel from six core agencies.
He said AKPS was prepared to open applications to other groups if the first two recruitment phases failed to achieve a reasonable staffing level. — Bernama
Editor’s note: AKPS is the Malay abbreviation for Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia.

86a74a4fb49be90b: SEGAMAT, Sept 27 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) needs its own world-class training academy to build expertise in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said today.
He said building in-house capabilities was crucial for preparing AKPS officers to tackle increasingly complex border security challenges and operate independently over the next 10 to 20 years.

“The world-class AKPS Training Academy is important for producing more talented and highly skilled Malaysians in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence, who are future-ready, uphold integrity and are committed to safeguarding national interests,” he said at the passing-out ceremony for the AKPS Basic Training Course Series 1/2026 at the Segamat Police Training Centre here.
Also present was AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Shamsul Azri said the proposed academy was part of AKPS’ plan to move beyond securing entry points towards smart, integrated and intelligence-led border control.

He said AKPS, currently in its first phase as “Guardians of Checkpoint”, must evolve from simply controlling the movement of people and goods at border crossings to taking a more proactive approach to border security.

“This is the change we must make — from guarding checkpoints to managing the border through smart, integrated and intelligence-led control, ultimately becoming the security leader for the country’s entire border ecosystem,” he said.

He said the agency’s human capital development must keep pace with technological advances and evolving criminal methods, with training continuing through on-the-job experience, exposure to real operations and mentoring by experienced officers.
Shamsul Azri said AKPS had made encouraging progress in its nearly 23 months of operation despite having only about 30 per cent of its optimum staffing level of 13,721 personnel.
He said the value of seizures and leakages prevented by AKPS this year had reached RM265 million, about three times the amount recorded in 2025.

He also highlighted AKPS’ success in returning 436 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin through cooperation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, Royal Malaysia Police, Department of Environment and port authorities.
The 408 pioneer AKPS officers who completed their three-month basic training today are the first batch to enter the public service under the new AKPS scheme, which took effect on July 1.

The batch comprises 39 assistant border superintendents and 369 border assistant officers, who will be stationed at the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link entry point from Oct 1 ahead of the service’s full operation on Jan 1, 2027. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: AKPS is the Malay abbreviation for Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia,.

bc26475675090572: From Jamaluddin Aziz
Mara chairman Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's call to end or restrict movies and dramas depicting bullying represents a familiar, knee-jerk reaction to deep-seated societal issues.

It is clear that while the anxiety surrounding youth violence in schools is entirely valid, the proposed censorship and blanket ban on creative narratives rests on an archaic understanding of how the media operates.
As media scholars, we have seen this script play out for over a century, and history has repeatedly proven that smashing the mirror does not cure the reflection.
To understand why this approach is fundamentally flawed, we must trace this anxiety back to the birth of media effects research in the early 20th century.
During the 1920s and 1930s, early theorists propagated what became known as the "Magic Bullet Theory" or the "Hypodermic Needle Theory".

This paradigm assumed that media messages were injected directly into a passive, helpless audience, immediately altering their behaviour and thoughts. It presumed that if a viewer saw violence on screen, they would inevitably replicate it on the streets.

By the 1940s, empirical research had thoroughly discredited this theory. Audiences are not a monolith, nor are they mindless vessels waiting to be programmed. Yet, the tradition of using the media as a convenient scapegoat for complex societal ills persists.

From comic books and rock music to video games and local cinema, authority figures have long favoured moral panics over structural analysis because blaming a screen is far easier than fixing a broken social fabric.

Crucially, the rapid evolution of media technology has completely transformed what it means to be an "audience". The very concept of "mass media" belonged to a bygone era of a one-to-many communication flow, a single broadcasting station transmitting to an uncritical mass. Today, that dynamic is dead.

The contemporary media landscape is highly decentralised and personalised. We no longer have passive consumers; we have "producers" who are individuals who simultaneously consume, critique, remix, and actively create content.
Modern audiences possess a sharp consciousness of their own individuality and exercise significant agency in how they interpret media.
Therefore, trying to eradicate bullying by banning a movie is a remarkably lazy policy response. It assumes a direct causal link that simply does not exist in a vacuum.

If the core fear is that a gullible audience will immediately mimic cinematic slang and adopt aggressive personas, we must look at the wider cultural landscape. Consider how the term "bossku" was enthusiastically adopted and chanted by political fans across the nation.

That phrase did not gain cultural dominance because of a movie script; it thrived because of real-world political dynamics, digital echo chambers, and active audience participation. Media does not dictate culture; it interacts with it.

To truly make sense of bullying and the bully, we must look beyond the screen. Banning stories about bullying only sanitises our media environment while leaving the actual victims unprotected in the real world.

We need to understand why bullying takes place, the psychological mechanisms behind peer pressure, and the systemic failures within our educational and familial institutions that allow aggression to go unchecked. To achieve this, we need rigorous data, not reactionary censorship.

I urge our relevant government agencies as well as the education; higher education; women, family and community development; and communications ministries to collaborate and offer substantial research grants dedicated to qualitative studies on youth deviance and bullying.
We must talk to the perpetrators, the victims, and the bystanders.

Only by conducting deep, qualitative research can we understand how bullies make sense of their own behaviour, how they rationalise their actions, and how subcultures form. Censorship is a temporary curtain; empirical understanding is the only real cure.
Let's stop blaming the filmmakers and start funding the solutions.
Jamaluddin Aziz is an associate professor in critical media studies at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's Centre for Research in Media and Communication and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
6377de91243db7f7: LIVERPOOL: Britain's ruling Labour Party gathers Sunday for its first annual conference under Andy Burnham's leadership, heartened by his start as prime minister but now looking for concrete plans to tackle looming challenges.
The former mayor of Manchester has injected new life into the centre-left party since MPs elevated him to Downing Street in July after ending Keir Starmer's two-year premiership.

Burnham's higher personal approval ratings, coupled with difficulties facing rival hard-right Reform UK, have helped Labour enter the conference ahead in some opinion polls, a sharp turnaround from the start of 2026.
"I think the mood will be buoyant," Labour MP Paula Barker said of the four-day gathering in the northwestern English city of Liverpool.
"Things are moving in a better direction than the last two years," she told AFP.

Last year's Labour conference was overshadowed by talk that Starmer's days were numbered, while the 2024 edition followed criticism of several government policy decisions made soon after the party won that year's election.

Since becoming prime minister on July 20, just weeks after returning to parliament following a nine-year absence, Burnham has sought to give voters some "breathing space" from cost-of-living pressures exacerbated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
He has cut electricity bills, capped bus fares, and reduced business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues.
Those measures, together with Burnham's active social-media presence, have helped strengthen his public image.
Surveys suggest that almost half of Britons view him favourably.
Burnham has also set up a "No 10 North" office in Manchester as part of his plans to spur GDP by devolving more powers to cities and regions.

However, he has said little about how he plans to fulfil pledges to end rough sleeping by homeless people, reform a ballooning welfare bill, fund a new social care service, reindustrialise the country and raise defence spending.
'Underlying anxiety'

Former minister Tony McNulty, who served alongside Burnham in Labour governments of the early 2000s, told AFP the premier must start fleshing out a promised "10-year plan for Britain" during his keynote speech at the conference on Tuesday.
"Much of it might still be broad brushstrokes but he needs to start the process of putting meat on the bone.
"It needs to go beyond the TikTok and good vibes stuff," he said.
Labour MP Alex Sobel told AFP he wants to hear "what we'll do to support" young people in terms of opportunities.
Some 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 are not in employment, training or education, statistics show.
Burnham has limited fiscal flexibility because of Labour's election-winning manifesto commitments to not raise income tax, national insurance contributions or value-added tax.
It makes finance minister John Healey's first budget on Oct 28 a difficult one.
Burnham told interviewers Friday that he would not call an early election before the required date of August 2029 to remove those red lines.
"All of this speculation on an early election, I can knock that dead," he told ITV.
Burnham said he wanted to focus on helping the public feel "a bit of hope in their lives again" and would use Tuesday's speech to "say further about the direction I want to take the country".
A YouGov poll published Thursday put support for Labour at 24% and Reform on 22%, a dramatic turnaround from last year when Nigel Farage's anti-immigrant group enjoyed double-digit leads.
If an election were held tomorrow, Labour would lose its majority but would likely be able to lead a progressive coalition, the survey suggested.
"There's still an underlying anxiety about how long ... (Labour's) bounce will last given the very tricky fiscal situation the government is in," political scientist Tim Bale told AFP.
"And the fact that Labour is still a long way off the 30% or so that's the minimum needed to ... win an election," Bale said.
c6c9287776661ab5: SEGAMAT: Attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers out of Malaysia are being foiled almost daily at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, with foreigners making up most of those detained, the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) said today.

Director Datuk Sri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the agency had stepped up targeted screening at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 following a recent incident involving a Malaysian pilot who was detained in Indonesia.

In July, the pilot was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg into the country. Indonesian authorities also seized 2.74g of methamphetamine and a further 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue.
Suhaily said almost every day, or at least every week, MCBA detained those attempting to smuggle cannabis flowers out of the country.

"Most are not Malaysians but foreigners," he told a press conference after the MCBA Basic Officer Training Course Series 1/2026 closing ceremony held at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) here today.
He said MCBA was tasked with coordinating screening with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at both KLIA terminals.
MCBA was also given three key responsibilities at international airports under 17 government initiatives to strengthen border security.
"The three main areas are coordinating targeted screening, intelligence matters and K9 operations at international airports.
"We are putting all these measures in place and the public will see them being implemented at airports," he said.
Meanwhile, the value of seizures and government revenue leakages foiled by MCBA has exceeded RM265 million so far this year, nearly triple the RM80 million recorded last year.
Shuhaily said e-waste and drug smuggling were among the main contributors to the figure.
He attributed the increase to strengthened enforcement, including new schemes and efforts to foster a stronger work culture among its personnel.
He said the measures would continue to be strengthened to tighten controls at the country's entry points and curb smuggling and revenue leakages.

Also present at the event were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid and Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad.
2d0d9629e8c09fa5: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd over losses incurred by the company in 2023.

The commission said the investigation covers several issues, including the development of a 50-megawatt solar project in Gambang, Pahang, for which a payment of RM42 million was reportedly made without the approval of the board of directors.
"The investigation is still ongoing due to the complexity of the case, which involves technical aspects, and is awaiting further instructions from the prosecution.

"To complete the investigation, MACC will also examine whether there are other relevant issues, including governance weaknesses, as highlighted by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim," MACC said in a statement today.
It said it welcomed the prime minister's concern and firm stance in addressing the weaknesses that contributed to the losses suffered by UiTM Holdings.
Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed that the investigation is being conducted under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.
He said MACC would complete the investigation swiftly, independently and fairly.
Yesterday, Anwar had directed Universiti Teknologi Mara to review UiTM Holdings' governance and management over concerns about the company's losses.
He had said the review should be conducted in cooperation with the UiTM vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister's Department, which would provide support where necessary.

He was responding to an audience member who wanted the government and the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation to review the management of UiTM Holdings, which the student claimed had recorded losses of more than RM100 million.
The issue was raised during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM in Shah Alam.
71a743a810e0b00c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — A signalling system disruption between Kalumpang and Kuala Kubu Bharu yesterday delayed KTM Komuter and ETS services by up to five hours.

In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said the worst KTM Komuter delay was recorded by Train No. 2389 at 230 minutes, while ETS service EP9138 from KL Sentral to Butterworth was delayed by 305 minutes.
Preliminary checks found that a damaged system component had disrupted the signalling system, although the cause of the damage is still being investigated.
“The signalling system disruption had a knock-on effect on the movement and schedules of other trains passing through the sector, particularly services to and from the north,” the statement read.
KTMB said scheduled Rawang-Ipoh Double Tracking upgrade works were also being carried out in stages along the affected route yesterday and today, requiring adjustments to train schedules.
The signalling fault during the works further restricted train movements and compounded delays to several KTM Komuter and ETS services, it said.
Repair works were completed at 5.15am today, with the first Komuter train from Tanjung Malim departing at 5.45am.

KTMB said KTM Komuter and ETS services have since returned to normal, although some trains remain subject to delays of up to 30 minutes from their original schedules due to the signalling fault along the Batang Kali route.

The national rail operator apologised to affected passengers and said full fare refunds would be given to those who chose not to continue their journey because of the disruption, subject to prevailing procedures. — Bernama
8718a9a79399a4ea: SEGAMAT: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) needs its own world-class training academy to produce highly skilled officers in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.

He said developing in-house capabilities was crucial to ensuring that MCBA was prepared to face increasingly complex border security challenges and had the capacity to operate independently over the next 10 to 20 years.

"The world-class MCBA Training Academy is important for producing more talented and highly skilled Malaysians in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence, who are future-ready, uphold integrity and are committed to safeguarding national interests," he said at the passing-out ceremony for the MCBA Basic Training Course Series 1/2026 at the Segamat Police Training Centre (Pulapol) today.
Also present was MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.

Shamsul Azri said the proposed academy was in line with MCBA's plans to move beyond a reactive approach focused on securing the country's entry points towards smart, integrated and intelligence-led border control.

He said MCBA, currently in its first phase as 'Guardians of Checkpoint', must go beyond simply controlling the movement of people and goods at border entry points and shift from a reactive to a proactive approach.

"This is the change we must make – from guarding checkpoints to managing the border through smart, integrated and intelligence-led control, ultimately becoming the security leader for the country's entire border ecosystem," he said.
He said the development of MCBA's human capital must keep pace with technological advances and ever-evolving criminal modus operandi.
Shamsul Azri said officers' training should not end at the training centre but continue through on-the-job training, exposure to real operational situations and mentoring by experienced officers.

He said MCBA had also made encouraging progress in the approximately 23 months since its establishment, despite currently operating with only about 30 per cent of its optimum staffing level of 13,721 personnel.
He said the value of seizures and leakages prevented by MCBA this year had reached RM265 million, about three times the amount recorded in 2025.

Shamsul Azri also expressed his appreciation for MCBA's success in sending 436 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) back to their countries of origin through collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, police, Department of Environment and port authorities.

Meanwhile, he said the 408 pioneer MCBA officers who completed their three-month basic training today were the first batch to enter the public service under the new MCBA scheme, which came into effect on July 1.

They comprise 39 Penolong Penguasa Sempadan (Grade KS5) and 369 Pembantu Penguasa Sempadan (Grade KS1), who will be stationed at the Johor Baru-Singapore RTS Link entry point from Oct 1 in preparation for the full operation of the service on Jan 1, 2027. — BERNAMA
d6874ce84fa88510: KUALA LUMPUR: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) futures contract is expected to attract bargain-hunting interest next week, supported by the extension of the US-China trade truce by another two months.

IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said the extension reduces the immediate risk of another round of tariff escalation before year-end and provides greater visibility for businesses and supply chains.
"Improved risk appetite following the extension of the trade truce could provide room for the index to rebound, although elevated oil prices and global bond yields remain key downside risks.

The index is also trading closer to its recent year-to-date low of 1,656.83, which could encourage selective bargain hunting in fundamentally strong large-cap counters following the recent pullback," he said in his daily market update on WhatsApp Channels.
However, Mohd Sedek reckons that any near-term recovery is likely to remain selective rather than broad-based, as investors continue to monitor global bond yields, oil prices and foreign fund flows.
The FBM KLCI futures ended lower this week, tracking the weaker underlying cash market.

On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the September 2026 contract gained 18.5 points to 1,661.5, while the October 2026 and March 2027 contracts both gained 12.5 points to 1,655.0 and 1,647.5, respectively. The December 2026 note added 14.5 points to 1,664.0.
Weekly turnover surged to 145,235 lots from 27,714 lots last week, while open interest spiked to 145,426 contracts on Friday from 48,164 contracts a week earlier.
Over the last week, the FBM KLCI increased 6.06 points to settle at 1,671.62 yesterday.
db63d166ff4a15a7: SHANGHAI: China said on Saturday it had agreed with the US on a US$30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement and on launching a dialogue on AI, under an eight-point consensus reached during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.
The two sides have also agreed to set up a trade council and extend the outcomes of earlier talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.

The agreement follows an earlier move by the world's two largest economies to extend by two months a trade truce that had been due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on ‌a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.

The three-day summit between Xi and President Donald Trump, which ended on Friday, showcased personal diplomacy rather than big public breakthroughs. Xi has since landed in Beijing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday.

On artificial intelligence, the two sides agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology's risks and benefits, with the next round of discussions set for November, and to set up a communication channel for AI-related incidents, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.

Beyond the economy, they also agreed to support each other in hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting and the Group of 20 summit, with both leaders planning to attend the gatherings hosted by the other, as Trump had earlier said in a social media post.

On foreign policy, the leaders agreed that Iran should fulfil its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons and that no country or entity should impose transit tolls on international waterways, the ministry said.
The US Embassy in Beijing did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
1dd73664c4650d2f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Indonesian actress Caitlin Halderman hopes her involvement in the horror drama series The Hidden Hand (Dia Perempuan Sialan), which marks her acting debut in Malaysia, will open doors for her to further develop her career in the country.

The 26-year-old actress said spending more than a month in Malaysia for the filming of the drama, in which she plays the character Riska, had made her increasingly comfortable with the local culture and way of life, while also sparking her desire to return for other projects in the country.
“I love working in Malaysia because the people here are very kind, and I would say the food here is also my comfort food. It feels like home.

“I had been to Malaysia about four years ago, but only for three days, so I did not really get to experience much. This time, I was able to experience the way Malaysians live,” she said when met after her appearance on the Fokus 30 programme, produced by Bernama Radio, at Wisma Bernama here yesterday.

The beautiful actress, who is of Dutch and Minangkabau heritage, said although there were some language challenges during filming, particularly because the original script was written in Bahasa Malaysia while her character is an Indonesian woman, the openness of the cast made her feel comfortable.
The 12-episode drama, which premiered on Sept 18 on the Viu video streaming platform, also stars Meerqeen, Hannah Delisha and Datin Seri Umie Aida.
Indonesian actress Caitlin Halderman speaks during her guest appearance on the ‘Fokus 30’ programme produced by Bernama Radio at Wisma Bernama September 25, 2026. — Bernama pic
Caitlin said everyone on the set was very open to sharing ideas and perspectives, as well as information about the Malaysian entertainment industry.

“I also shared with them about the Indonesian industry. We discussed things almost every day and there were no barriers among us, except for the language. But it was not a problem because every day I would ask how to adapt the dialogue in the script into Indonesian,” she said.
Caitlin said the possession scenes were among the most challenging parts of the filming as they required greater physical energy and emotional intensity.

“Those scenes were something I had never done before, so for me, they were the most difficult. Horror stories require a lot of emotion and energy because there are action scenes, possession scenes and so on,” she said.

She added that her experience as a former water polo athlete had also helped her considerably in her acting career, particularly in developing discipline, patience and the stamina to remain physically active.
Caitlin said her entry into acting was unplanned as she had initially tried her hand at an audition for a brand commercial.
“I was selected. After that, I was asked to audition for a film and was selected again. That was when I thought that this was quite fun, being part of this industry,” she said.

The Hidden Hand follows Riska, a woman determined to seek revenge against a family she believes was responsible for destroying her mother’s life. She infiltrates the family by disguising herself as a domestic helper. — Bernama
bd0d3149136cbe69: KOTA BARU: A Jeep Wrangler worth nearly RM500,000 belonging to a popular Kelantan businesswoman was among 3,790 luxury vehicles seized by the Road Transport Department nationwide under Op Luxury.
Its senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the vehicle was seized in Jalan Taman Tengku Anis here at about 2.50pm on Sept 24.
He added that the jeep was seized after it was found to have an expired motor vehicle licence.
He said the 3,790 vehicles were seized between June 2025 and Sept 26 this year, with an estimated value of RM550 million.
"The operation is a continuation of Op Luxury, which has been carried out since last year to tackle serious offences involving luxury vehicle owners.
"Among the main offences detected are failure to renew road tax and insurance, driving without a valid licence and other offences," he told a press conference here today.
Of the total, Kifli said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December last year, while another 3,005 were seized from Jan 1 to Sept 26 this year.
"Negri Sembilan recorded the highest number of seizures with 469 vehicles, followed by Selangor (410), Kuala Lumpur (382), Johor (367) and Penang (357)," he added.
He said enforcement was intensified after the department found that some luxury vehicle owners had failed to renew their road tax for years.
He said the most common reason given by owners was that they were reluctant to renew their road tax because their vehicles had been blacklisted due to previous offences or outstanding summonses.
"Some claimed they had previous offences, such as failing to comply with speed limits, or other outstanding summonses.
"What shocked us was that even lower-income vehicle owners were able to renew their road tax, while some luxury vehicle owners, who are generally from the T20 group, had failed to do so," he said.
He said the department had found cases where road tax had not been renewed for many years, including records dating back to 2014 and 2020.
Kifli said the vehicles seized ranged from supercars worth more than RM1 million, with the most expensive valued at RM8.8 million, to luxury vehicles worth between RM250,000 and RM1 million.
He said the number of supercars involved had declined, while vehicles in the RM250,000 to RM1 million range, including BMWs, Toyota Alphards and Toyota Vellfires, remained common.
He said more than 20 per cent of the 3,790 vehicles seized were linked to owners categorised as T20 based on the department's investigations and various indicators.
He said the group included entrepreneurs, particularly those in the cosmetics business, traders and influencers.
Kifli also said the department had detected cases involving owners of two or three vehicles using the same registration number, which resulted in additional offences being recorded.

He said the enforcement action had also contributed to government revenue, with the department collecting about RM35 million last year from summons payments and motor vehicle licence-related payments.

2b2a09a3ea6ce58a: WHILE thousands of motorsport fans will descend on Sepang for the Formula 1 action, there is another side of the district where the pace is considerably slower - one measured by sunsets, fishing boats and the ebb and flow of the tide.

At Pantai Bagan Lalang, just about 30 minutes away from the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), the sound of waves replaces roaring engines as campers pitch their tents along the coast, drawn by the beach's open views and its location at the meeting point of the sea and river.
As evening approaches, the sky over the Malacca Strait shifts into vibrant shades of orange, pink, and purple, making it a premier spot for sunset watchers.
For Chef Yang, 56, who has lived in Sepang since 2000, the beach has become a regular camping ground over the past five years.
"I camp almost every day," she said, adding that she preferred Bagan Lalang because of its location at the estuary, where she can watch the sunset and observe fishing boats coming and going.
"Here, you can see the fishermen heading out and returning at around 3am or 4am. You can see them lined up as they leave. This beach has its own uniqueness."
A retired chef who now organises events and develops recipes and camping modules, Chef Yang often camps alone, although she said the nature of camping meant she rarely remained a stranger for long.

"Even if you come alone, God will send people your way. Friends you don't know will arrive and become friends," she said, adding that Pantai Bagan Lalang is usually full of campers during the weekends and public holidays.
Her connection with the outdoors has also shaped how she spends her time at Bagan Lalang.
While the beach is not suitable for swimming, visitors can take part in activities such as night crab spotting, fishing and looking for oysters.
She and a friend also regularly clear rubbish and debris from the area, particularly as some campers may not realise that fallen wood and other material should not simply be burned.
The beach also attracts groups of motorhome owners, who make it a regular weekend destination, often arriving on Fridays and staying until Sunday.
Mohd Azmi Suito, 60, is another regular camper who prefers the freedom of deciding where to go and pitching his tent wherever he finds a place that feels right.
"I usually go wherever I feel like going. Wherever I stop, that's where I camp," he said.
For him, the sea offers a sense of calm, while camping in a natural setting allows him to meet fellow campers and exchange stories.
"I don't like complicated places. I prefer somewhere natural like this. When you meet people, they share stories and you forget, for a while, about the things you're going through," he said.
He said he also appreciated the quiet atmosphere at Pantai Bagan Lalang and would sometimes stay longer when he found the surroundings particularly peaceful.
2a1edad316b63cf8: PETALING JAYA: Siasatan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) berhubung kerugian RM157 juta yang dialami UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd dalam tempoh empat tahun masih dijalankan berikutan kerumitan kes itu.
Ketua Pesuruhjaya SPRM, Abd Halim Aman, berkata siasatan itu melibatkan perkara teknikal yang kompleks, selain agensi antirasuah itu masih menunggu arahan lanjut daripada pihak pendakwaan.
Antara perkara yang disiasat ialah pembayaran RM42 juta berkaitan projek solar berkapasiti 50MW di Gambang, Pahang.
Halim berkata wang itu dipercayai digunakan untuk tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek solar berkenaan, manakala pembayaran itu dibuat tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah UiTM Holdings.
Beliau berkata kes itu disiasat mengikut Seksyen 23 Akta SPRM 2009, yang melibatkan penggunaan jawatan atau kedudukan untuk mendapatkan suapan.
“Kita akan berusaha sedaya upaya untuk melengkapkan siasatan secepat mungkin secara bebas dan adil,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Beliau berkata SPRM turut meneliti sama ada terdapat isu lain, termasuk kelemahan dalam pengurusan UiTM Holdings, susulan kebimbangan yang dibangkitkan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim semalam.
Pada 2023, SPRM memulakan siasatan terhadap kerugian RM157 juta yang dialami UiTM Holdings bagi 2017, 2018, 2019 dan 2021.
Ketika itu, SPRM berkata pihaknya meneliti beberapa pelaburan yang dibuat syarikat berkenaan bagi menentukan sama ada wujud unsur rasuah, salah guna kuasa atau penyelewengan dana.
Semalam, Anwar mengarahkan Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) mengkaji semula tadbir urus dan pengurusan cabang pelaburannya susulan kerugian berjuta-juta ringgit yang dialami.
9a268e143cb1d75f: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aquatics diving technical director Yeoh Ken Nee hopes Elvis Priestly Clement and Enrique Maccartney Harold can build on their Asian Games silver by qualifying for the men's 10m platform synchro at the Olympic Games.

The Malaysians scored 377.52 points yesterday to claim the country's first silver in the event in 16 years, edging South Korea's Shin Jung Whi–Kim Young Taek by just 1.62 points at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre.
Ken Nee now hopes the pair can take their partnership to the Olympic stage.
"Moving forward, I hope they can qualify for this event at the (2028) Olympic Games," he said.
The medal came down to the final dive.
South Korea led by 0.54 points after five rounds, but Elvis–Enrique produced their best dive of the contest when it mattered most, scoring 81.00 points.
The Koreans needed 80.46 points from their last dive to draw level. They scored 78.84 and settled for bronze with 375.90 points.
China's Yang Hao–Lian Jun Jie took gold with 465.54 points.
Ken Nee praised the pair's confidence throughout the final.
"This is one of their favourite events, and they showed good confidence and consistency throughout the competition," Ken Nee said of Elvis and Enrique.
"I'm very happy with their performance and the effort they put in today. Overall, they did a great job."
Enrique has no more events, while Elvis will next compete in the individual 10m platform preliminaries alongside Bertrand Rhodict Lises on Wednesday.
76d0f8b0625c52ca: KUALA LUMPUR: UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd already has a recovery plan and proposals to address its financial position following accumulated losses of RM157 million, said its chairman Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya.
He said the recovery plan and proposals had been presented several times through governance channels, including to the university's Board of Directors.
"What is needed now is alignment, decision-making and implementation across the entire UiTM ecosystem," he said in a post on Facebook yesterday.
Fathul Bari said he acknowledged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's concerns over the losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Group.
"I appreciate the concern and firmness shown by the prime minister. This attention should serve as momentum to strengthen the recovery process already underway.
"However, the facts need to be placed within their proper timeline. The losses being referred to are not new losses incurred under the current leadership.
"The figure of RM157 million has been reported since 2023 and the Higher Education Ministry at the time explained that it represented accumulated losses dating back to 2007.
"The issue was also examined in the 2022 Auditor General's Report and through Public Accounts Committee (PAC) proceedings, followed by the tabling of the PAC report in 2024.
"These are the chronological facts. This is a legacy issue."
He said the past losses had created a trust deficit in UiTM Holdings.

"But a trust deficit should not be passed on indefinitely to a new leadership. The leadership has since changed, while governance is being strengthened. Therefore, the performance of the current leadership should be assessed based on its integrity, implementation and results."
He said the new leadership was determined to restore performance, strengthen governance, rebuild confidence and put UiTM Holdings back on a growth trajectory.
"We are not using legacy issues as an excuse. We are identifying those legacy issues in order to resolve them."
He also hoped that the issue would not be politicised by any party.

"This is not a political issue. This is about restoring an asset owned by the university. If UiTM Holdings is strengthened, the value will ultimately return to UiTM. If it remains weak, UiTM will also bear the consequences."

In the post, Fathul Bari also proposed that the prime minister, particularly in his capacity as finance minister, consider a national framework under which university holding companies and subsidiaries would be given a First Right of Refusal for suitable business opportunities within their respective university ecosystems, subject fully to merit, due diligence, competitiveness and good governance.
"This is not about free projects, nor is it about monopolies. It is about having the first opportunity to compete and be assessed professionally.
"If university companies are capable of undertaking such opportunities competitively, it would be more strategic for the economic value generated to remain within the university ecosystem.
"The profits of university subsidiaries should ultimately be channelled back towards strengthening the university."
Yesterday, Anwar directed Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to review UiTM Holdings' governance and management over concerns about the company's losses.
Anwar said the review should be conducted in cooperation with the UiTM vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister's Department, which would provide support where necessary.
The issue was raised during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM, here.

4dff66e097f6ec52: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he will hold a meeting tonight with Negeri Sembilan assemblymen from Barisan Nasional (BN), PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara tonight in a fresh attempt to resolve the state’s ongoing constitutional crisis.

The meeting at Menara Dato’ Onn here will focus on coordinating the parties and identifying possible solutions in line with the state Constitution and customs, national news agency Bernama reported this afternoon.

“The meeting is for me to coordinate, with no intention of interfering, but to find the best solution to the crisis currently faced by Negeri Sembilan,” Zahid was quoted as telling reporters after officiating the 18th Malaysian Makkal Sakti Party General Assembly here yesterday.
Zahid, who is BN chairman, said any solution must put the interests of the people first while respecting the state’s laws, Constitution and customs.

He also gave Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim full mandate to seek a way forward, including seeking an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, the four Undangs and Tunku Besar Tampin.
Zahid was also asked about the possibility of declaring a political emergency in Negeri Sembilan.

“I do not think we should move towards that because there has been no disturbance to peace in Negeri Sembilan, and there is no need to even consider such a thing... there must surely be better options,” he was quoted as saying.
The latest move comes amid a widening dispute between the state government and palace over the authority to revoke the appointments of the 10 state executive council members.
Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments effective Sept 20 after the palace said the exco members had breached their oaths of office, while Ismail has disputed the validity of the move.
The Attorney-General has said the revocation was valid under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, while the former exco members have since been barred from entering their offices.
8ca9c150e2830f6b: THE roar of Formula 1 (F1) cars will return to Sepang after a seven-year absence, but for residents and businesses in the district, the race for economic gains may begin well before the chequered flag falls.

When the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix takes place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2-4, thousands of motorsport fans, racing teams and international visitors are expected to descend on the district.

Sepang member of parliament Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the race's return was expected to generate significant economic spillover for Sepang and surrounding areas, particularly in tourism, hospitality, transport, food and beverage, and small businesses.

"An international event of this scale has the potential to generate significant economic value of hundreds of millions, with the benefits extending not only to major industries but also to ordinary people who depend on daily business activities.

"The multiplier effect is expected to be felt through increased demand for hotels, homestays, rental apartments, transport services, restaurants, food stalls and various supporting businesses," she told the New Straits Times.
The ripple effect, she said, could extend beyond Sepang to Cyberjaya, Putrajaya and the wider Klang Valley as visitors look for places to stay, eat and explore.
She said this was also in line with the momentum of Visit Malaysia 2026, which aims to increase international tourist arrivals.
"F1 is not merely a racing event, but a platform to promote Malaysia, particularly Sepang, as a world-class tourism destination," she said.
The aim, she added, was to encourage visitors to stay longer, spend locally and discover the district beyond its famous racing circuit.

Sepang's attractions include Bagan Lalang's coastline, Sungai Pelek's agricultural offerings, mangrove ecosystems along the Sepang River and the Mah Meri Orang Asli community, alongside traditional villages and community-based tourism offerings.
Aiman Athirah said supporting programmes such as carnivals, cultural activities and tourism promotions could encourage visitors to extend their stays and spend in surrounding areas.

"Most importantly, these economic benefits must reach the people. We want small businesses, food-stall operators, local restaurants, homestay operators, e-hailing drivers, handicraft entrepreneurs and the service sector to also benefit from this historic event," she said.
A Dragon Fruit Economy
One of Sepang's biggest local stories, however, is its dragon fruit fields.
The drive from SIC towards Bagan Lalang offers a glimpse of an agricultural economy that has become closely associated with the district, with dragon fruit stalls and farms lining the roads.
Pitaya cultivation in Sepang now covers 480 hectares and involves 265 farmers, with annual production estimated at 12,000 tonnes.

Aiman Athirah said the 2023 Agriculture Census showed Sepang was Malaysia's largest dragon fruit-producing district, recording 18,779.8 tonnes of production - ahead of other major producing districts such as Batu Pahat and Kluang.
The district also recorded the country's highest sales volume, at 15,047.1 tonnes.
"This shows that dragon fruit is no longer merely a side crop or small-scale farm produce.
"It has become an economic activity with commercial value and significant potential to be developed as a local agro-industry," she said.
For Aiman Athirah, that is exactly the kind of story Sepang should be able to tell when the world arrives for Formula 1.

"We do not want visitors to come to Sepang only because of F1, Kuala Lumpur International Airport or its beaches. We want them to know Sepang through its produce, food, farms and the communities behind them.
"F1 brings the world to Sepang. Dragon fruit, meanwhile, can bring Sepang's story to the world," she said.
More Than A Race
Aiman Athirah hopes the return of Formula 1 will also mark a new chapter for Malaysia on the global motorsport stage.

F1, she said, could help strengthen Malaysia's international image, attract high-quality tourists, create economic opportunities, promote technology and engineering, and inspire the younger generation.
"We want this event to leave a bigger legacy for the people, not just be an event lasting a few days, but become a catalyst for Sepang's economic development and global brand.
"We want that when the chequered flag is raised in Sepang, the world will see not just a race, but a Malaysia that is ready, progressive and capable of becoming a world-class host," she said.
Aiman Athirah said the government is also taking a comprehensive and coordinated approach to ensure the event runs smoothly and safely.
Preparations extend beyond SIC to the wider event ecosystem, including road infrastructure, traffic management, security and emergency response, cleanliness, public facilities and visitor management.
They also cover community participation and the readiness of Sepang's tourism and local economic sectors, with efforts aimed at ensuring the benefits of the event extend beyond the circuit itself.

eff621082e35d958: FORMULA 1's return to Sepang is more than a revival of high-octane racing - it could unleash up to RM1.3 billion in economic activity across Malaysia.
The event could revive a potentially lucrative tourism and business platform nearly a decade after F1 cars last roared around the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), industry observers said.
The one-off race, which replaces the cancelled Bahrain Grand Prix and is scheduled for Oct 2-4, will provide additional lift to tourism-related service industries, they added.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) estimates the race could generate RM1.1 billion-RM1.3 billion in total economic output, driven mainly by visitor spending across tourism-related services.
HLIB expects an average spending of RM8,879 by an F1 tourist, reflecting the sport's relatively affluent international fan base.
The economic opportunity is particularly significant because Malaysia is not bearing the usual F1 hosting cost.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently said Bahrain had agreed to absorb the substantial registration and hosting fees, leaving Malaysia to spend up to RM16 million on minor track repairs.
That contrasts sharply with the economics of hosting F1 as a permanent fixture, which was one of the reasons Malaysia ended its 19-year run after the 2017 race.
Unlike Malaysia's previous full-season host tenure from 1999 to 2017, Bahrain will fully absorb the Formula One Management licence fee for this rescheduled race.

SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif recently said unlike Malaysia's 1999-2017 tenure as a full-season host, Bahrain will absorb the F1 rights fee of US$70 million-US$80 million (RM285 million-RM326 million).
This limits Malaysia's responsibility to only an estimated RM40 million in costs of local preparations to ensure the circuit meets F1 specifications.
Under the current arrangement, Bahrain would receive all ticket sales revenue while Malaysia will benefit from tourism spending spillover effects.
Rare Opportunity
Former SIC chief executive Datuk Razlan Razali said he had seen first hand the economic and tourism impact an F1 weekend could generate for Malaysia and Sepang during his tenure from 2008 to 2020.

"Beyond the spectacle on track, an F1 race brings significant economic spillover, hotel occupancy, tourism, F&B, logistics and media exposure that puts Malaysia on the global map for weeks, not just race day," he said when contacted.

Razlan said Sepang had world-class infrastructure built for F1-grade racing, and a return to the calendar could reconnect Malaysia with the sport while giving a new generation of fans the opportunity to experience F1 at home.
"The return of F1 next month is an exceptional situation to the advantage of Malaysia and Sepang," he said.
However, Razlan cautioned that bringing F1 back on an annual basis would require careful strategic planning and coordination across government ministries.
"Reality is that the cost to bring and host F1 annually is very expensive and careful strategic planning must be considered, presented and all Ministries must be involved," he said.
Razlan expects Malaysia and F1's commercial rights holder Formula One Management to hold discussions on the future of the race and whether it could eventually return to the permanent calendar.
"We have to make a strong case for it for the government to be convinced," he said.
HLIB hosting F1 required significant financial commitments from both the government and SIC.
The government, through the Finance Ministry, channelled financial grants to SIC for the payment of hosting rights fees and broadcasting rights fees.
Other fees including advertising rights fees, airtime management fees and hospitality rights fees were borne entirely by SIC.
Apart from hosting F1, Malaysia has also hosted other events such as MotoGP.

Between 1999 and 2012, the total cost of hosting F1 and MotoGP amounted to RM2.5 billion (about RM195 million a year). Of this, government grants totalled RM1.9 billion, accounting for 74 per cent of overall expenditure, while SIC financed the remaining RM661.8 million (26 per cent).
The financial burden increased over time as F1 hosting rights were contractually subject to annual increase of between five and 10 per cent, HLIB said.
Subsequently, government funding rose further to RM789.6 million (about RM263 million a year) during 2013-2015, with F1 accounting for largest share of total funding.
Tourism Benchmark
The last Malaysian Grand Prix in 2017 provided a useful benchmark for the potential tourism impact.
About 200,000 international visitors were attracted to Malaysia for the 2017 event, according to figures cited by tourism analysts.
The race was part of Malaysia's wider tourism ecosystem, generating spending across hotels, restaurants, transportation, retail and entertainment.
A PwC economic impact study commissioned by SIC in 2013 estimated that the 2012 Malaysian Grand Prix generated more than RM300 million in economic benefits and created more than 4,500 jobs.
The study also highlighted the extensive international media exposure generated by the race.

The RM300 million figure, however, should not be treated as the economic impact of the 2017 race itself. It was an estimate from the earlier 2012 event and provides historical context rather than a direct comparison with the latest HLIB projection.
Tourism A Big-Ticket Sector
The potential spillover from F1 comes at a time when tourism has become an increasingly important component of Malaysia's economy.
In 2017, the tourism industry contributed 14.9 per cent to the economy, with direct tourism gross domestic product (GDP) contribution reaching RM82.6 billion, according to the Statistics Department.

Inbound tourism expenditure accounted for 53.7 per cent of total tourism consumption, while shopping, accommodation and passenger transportation were the biggest components of inbound tourist spending.
Malaysia received 25.95 million international tourist arrivals in 2017 and recorded RM82.2 billion in tourist receipts, according to Tourism Malaysia.

This provides a broader context for the F1 contribution: the race itself was only one component of a much larger tourism economy, but its concentration of high-spending visitors over a single weekend made it particularly valuable to hospitality and services businesses.
Singapore Shows What F1 Can Deliver
The regional benchmark is Singapore, which has used its F1 race as a broader tourism and entertainment platform.

The republic's Trade and Industry Ministry said the Singapore Grand Prix had attracted more than 720,000 international visitors and generated more than S$2.2 billion in incremental tourism receipts from its inception in 2008 through 2024.
The comparison highlights an important distinction for Malaysia.

The economic value of F1 is not simply the number of people entering a circuit. It depends on how effectively visitors are encouraged to stay longer, spend beyond the venue and explore destinations outside the immediate race area.
From Sepang To The Wider Economy
Sepang and its surrounding areas could reap the biggest opportunity from the 2026 race.

Sepang is located close to Kuala Lumpur International Airport but outside the capital's main tourism areas. If visitors spend only a few days around the circuit, much of the economic benefit could remain concentrated in hotels, restaurants and transport services in the immediate area.

Packaging race attendance with Kuala Lumpur accommodation, shopping, food, cultural attractions and domestic destinations could extend visitor stays and spread spending across a wider group of businesses.
The race could also provide an additional platform for Malaysia to showcase its tourism offering during Visit Malaysia 2026.
F1's Value Extends Beyond Tourism
The economic spillover also goes beyond visitor spending.
Malaysia already has a deep commercial and technological connection to F1 through Petronas, which has maintained its partnership with the Mercedes-AMG Formula 1 team.

That relationship has increasingly focused on technology and the development of more sustainable fuels, creating potential links between motorsport research, energy technology and broader commercial applications.

F1 can similarly provide exposure for Malaysia's engineering, manufacturing, automotive and technology capabilities, although the scale of those benefits would depend on how much local industry can participate in the wider ecosystem.
The 2026 race therefore gives Malaysia an unusual opportunity to measure F1's economic value without taking on the full cost of a conventional long-term hosting arrangement.
Malaysia previously faced annual hosting fees of about RM300 million, with a three to five-year commitment potentially costing RM900 million-RM1.5 billion.
The government had ruled out a return under those economics as recently as 2025.
This time, the equation is different.

With Malaysia's direct spending capped at about RM16 million for track repairs and Bahrain covering the hosting and registration fees, the country can use the event as a real-world test of how much visitor spending, tourism promotion, business activity and international exposure F1 can generate.
The key number may therefore not be the crowd at Sepang or the television audience, but how much economic activity the race leaves behind after the chequered flag.
For Malaysia, the 2026 Grand Prix could provide the clearest data yet on whether F1 is primarily a costly sporting spectacle or a platform capable of generating wider economic returns.

7e21541b064dcc5e: DUBLIN: Ireland's football team voted on Saturday to fulfil a Nations League tie with Israel despite goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulling out of the match due to unease over the war in Gaza.

"We carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures," Football Association of Ireland (FAI) head David Courell told reporters in Debrecen, Hungary, where the game will take place today.
"It was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.
"Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football, that this fixture would continue as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures," he added.
Ireland are scheduled to play two Nations League ties against Israel, with the first – officially Israel's home fixture - at the neutral venue in Hungary.
Ireland's designated home match on October 4 has been moved from Dublin's Aviva Stadium to Backa Topola, Serbia, following concerns over disruption and security.
"I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly," Bolton's Bazunu said on Instagram.

"I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel. My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong," the 24-year-old added.
Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country's own history of British rule.
Dublin, alongside Spain and Norway, formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.
Israel strongly rejects allegations its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.
"Football has won, the separation between football and politics must be maintained," said a statement by the Israeli FA later Saturday hailing the Irish decision.
"The ones who have certainly lost today are those who wanted to intimidate, to separate and to turn the football pitch into a political arena," it added.

Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel, prominent Irish figures including sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have protested against the ties going ahead.
Bazunu's decision triggered the delay of a scheduled press conference on Saturday, followed by a vote among the squad on whether to fulfil the fixture or not.
"Nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons," said Ireland's Icelandic manager Heimir Hallgrimsson.
"We are trying to tackle it in the best way we can at the moment," he added.
Ireland players will not fulfil any media duties tomorrow, or against Austria in Dublin on October 1, or around the game against Israel in Serbia three days later, said Courell.
The players will wear black armbands "for all lives lost in the conflict" during Sunday's match, with profits from the Austria game to be donated to charity, he said.
Sunday's match comes days after national broadcaster RTE confirmed Ireland would again boycott the Eurovision Song Contest next year because of Israel's participation.
In a rare move for a state broadcaster, RTE said earlier it will show the Israel game without Irish commentary or pundits. - AFP

46badfa301c60930: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's (BN) cooperation with other parties at the federal level does not determine its political strategy at the state level, said BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

The state will hold its 16th election for the 28-seat legislative assembly, whose current term is due to expire on Dec 27.
