10c0e25b9ce53112: KUALA LUMPUR: A signalling system disruption between Kalumpang and Kuala Kubu Bharu yesterday left KTM Komuter and ETS services delayed by up to five hours.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said KTM Komuter Train No. 2389 was delayed by 230 minutes, while ETS service EP9138 (KL Sentral-Butterworth) had a 305-minute delay.

KTMB said preliminary checks traced the disruption to damage in a system component, which sparked and disrupted the signalling system. However, the cause of the component damage is still under investigation.
"The signalling system disruption had a knock-on effect on the movement and schedules of other trains passing through the sector, particularly services to and from the north," the statement read.

KTMB said the Rawang-Ipoh double-tracking upgrading works, scheduled earlier, were being carried out in stages, including along the Kalumpang route yesterday and today, requiring schedule adjustments on the affected line.
"The signalling disruption during these works further restricted train movements, compounding delays to several KTM Komuter and ETS services," the statement read.
However, KTMB said repair works were completed at 5.15am today, and the first Komuter train from Tanjung Malim departed at 5.45am.

The national rail operator said KTM Komuter and ETS services had now returned to normal, though a 30-minute delay from the original schedule persists due to the signalling fault along the Batang Kali route.

KTMB apologised to affected passengers for the incident, adding that full fare refunds will be given to those who chose not to continue their journey following the disruption, subject to prevailing procedures.
3f4b50196a32688e: LONDON: France forward Kylian Mbappe has suffered hyperextension of the left knee, his club Real Madrid said on Saturday.
The France captain has left the national team, having been forced to come off shortly after scoring the winner in Friday's 1-0 Nations League victory over Turkiye.

The 27-year-old was treated after the goal and briefly returned to the pitch but went down again moments later and was unable to continue, prompting France coach Zinedine Zidane to replace him in the 58th minute of his first game in charge.

"After the tests carried out today on our player Kylian Mbappe by Real Madrid's Medical Services, he has been diagnosed with a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee," read the statement.
The French Football Federation initially said Mbappe was suffering from a "knee tendon injury" and had returned to Madrid for further assessment.
Real next host Villarreal in LaLiga on October 10. - REUTERS
5e859f33be715bb0: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has urged Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to seek an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and the four Undangs to find a way out of the state’s constitutional crisis.

Zahid, who is also Umno president, said he had asked Ismail to engage the state’s traditional chieftains and seek an amicable solution in accordance with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and state customs, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported this afternoon.
“Most importantly, the people must be prioritised. Whatever has happened, has happened. Now, we should look for the best way to resolve the crisis.
“We definitely do not want the situation to worsen and for the people to be victimised by this,” he was quoted as telling reporters at the World Trade Centre here.

Zahid also acknowledged Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke the appointments of the 10 state executive councillors, saying the immediate priority was to ensure the state administration could continue serving the people.
Zahid stressed that he was not seeking to interfere in the state administration but wanted the dispute resolved amicably.
The crisis escalated after the state executive council (exco) issued a statement last week purportedly affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, which Ismail endorsed a day later.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers subsequently said the declaration was invalid, stating that neither the menteri besar nor the executive council have the authority to remove the state Ruler.
Tuanku Muhriz then revoked the appointments of all 10 exco members effective September 20, with the palace saying they had breached their oaths of office and pledge of allegiance to the ruler.
The revocation was gazetted on September 24.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar subsequently said the move was valid under Article XXXVIII(5) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution.
Ismail has disputed the revocation, asserting that the Ruler could not terminate the exco members without his advice or request and maintaining the validity of the current state government line-up.
The former exco members were subsequently barred from entering their offices, while police are also due to record their statements in connection with the ongoing dispute.
f8fa2ae241f18d87: KANGAR: A postage stamp can be a gateway for younger generations to discover history, geography, culture, science and even international relations, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said it was important for philately to continue evolving and find new ways to engage younger generations.

"While we must embrace new technologies and new forms of communication, we should not lose sight of the educational and historical value of our traditional forms of communication," he said in his speech at the opening ceremony of The Five-Nation Stamp Exhibition Perlis, Malaysia 2026 at Dewan 2020 here last night.
Raja of Perlis Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail officiated at the exhibition.
Also in attendance were the Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail and Raja Puan Muda of Perlis Tuanku Dr Hajah Lailatul Shahreen Akashah Khalil.
Fahmi said he was encouraged by the cooperation between his ministry and the Education Ministry, as well as efforts to introduce younger Malaysians to stamp collecting and philately.
He said the ministry recognised that preserving the country's postal and philatelic heritage required cooperation among many parties.

"As such, I commend the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, Pos Malaysia and the Philatelic Society of Malaysia for their respective roles in supporting and developing Malaysia's philatelic ecosystem.
"I also congratulate the Philatelic Society of Malaysia for bringing an international exhibition of this nature to Perlis," he said.

He said the history of postage stamps was closely connected with the history of communications itself and, for generations, the postal service was one of the most important means through which people, communities and nations remained connected.
"Every letter carried a message, and every stamp attached to it became part of that journey. Today, the way we communicate has changed dramatically.

"A message that once took days or weeks to arrive can now reach the other side of the world almost instantly. Yet, even in this digital age, postage stamps continue to have a special place in our society," he said.
Fahmi said stamps had evolved beyond their original postal function to become miniature records of national history and identity.

He said Malaysian stamps had commemorated significant national events, the Royal Institutions, distinguished personalities, cultural heritage, achievements, as well as the country's remarkable biodiversity.
"In this sense, stamps provide future generations with a visual record of who we are and the milestones we have achieved as a nation," he said.
d0626b96eff86b76: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) has called for the minimum wage to be raised to RM3,100 under the 2027 budget, saying current workers' salaries have yet to keep pace with productivity and company profits.

MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor also called for government- linked companies (GLC) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to lead the way in paying better wages before the private sector is pushed to do the same.
“Fair wages must start with GLCs and GLICs. It should not be only the top management that benefits while workers at the bottom are left with the scraps,” he said in a statement.

Kamarul welcomed Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s criticism of large corporations that continued paying low wages despite making huge profits, saying workers who helped generate those profits deserved a fairer share.
Yesterday, Anwar said the 2027 budget will include measures aimed at boosting the wage levels for workers in the private sector in line with growing productivity.

Anwar, who is also finance minister, said his administration will seek ways to negotiate with the private sector to raise wages in line with productivity levels, rather than threatening legal repercussions.

Since May 2025, six GLICs have set a minimum wage of RM3,100 for permanent employees as part of implementing a living wage policy. They are Khazanah Nasional Bhd, Permodalan Nasional Bhd, EPF, Retirement Fund Inc, the Armed Forces Fund Board and Lembaga Tabung Haji.
Anwar told Parliament last year that a total of 34 GLCs and GLICs have adopted the RM3,100 living wage policy.
The current minimum wage is RM1,700 a month.
The prime minister was also reported to have said that the RM1,700 minimum wage should not be treated as the starting salary for skilled workers or graduates.
bddf6d1eeb8a523f: LIVERPOOL, Sept 27 — Britain’s ruling Labour Party gathers today for its first annual conference under Andy Burnham’s leadership, heartened by his start as prime minister but now looking for concrete plans to tackle looming challenges.
The former mayor of Manchester has injected new life into the centre-left party since MPs elevated him to Downing Street in July after ending Keir Starmer’s two-year premiership.

Burnham’s higher personal approval ratings, coupled with difficulties facing rival hard-right Reform UK, have helped Labour enter the conference ahead in some opinion polls, a sharp turnaround from the start of 2026.
“I think the mood will be buoyant,” Labour MP Paula Barker said of the four-day gathering in the northwestern English city of Liverpool.
“Things are moving in a better direction than the last two years,” she told AFP.

Last year’s Labour conference was overshadowed by talk that Starmer’s days were numbered, while the 2024 edition followed criticism of several government policy decisions made soon after the party won that year’s election.

Since becoming prime minister on July 20, just weeks after returning to parliament following a nine-year absence, Burnham has sought to give voters some “breathing space” from cost-of-living pressures exacerbated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
He has cut electricity bills, capped bus fares, and reduced business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues.
Those measures, together with Burnham’s active social-media presence, have helped strengthen his public image.
Surveys suggest that almost half of Britons view him favourably.
Burnham has also set up a “No. 10 North” office in Manchester as part of his plans to spur GDP by devolving more powers to cities and regions.

But he has said little about how he plans to fulfil pledges to end rough sleeping by homeless people, reform a ballooning welfare bill, fund a new social care service, reindustrialise the country and raise defence spending.
‘Underlying anxiety’

Former minister Tony McNulty, who served alongside Burnham in Labour governments of the early 2000s, told AFP the premier must start fleshing out a promised “10-year plan for Britain” during his keynote speech at the conference on Tuesday.
“Much of it might still be broad brushstrokes but he needs to start the process of putting meat on the bone.
“It needs to go beyond the TikTok and good vibes stuff,” he said.
Labour MP Alex Sobel told AFP he wants to hear “what we’ll do to support” young people in terms of opportunities.
Some 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 are not in employment, training or education, statistics show.
Burnham has limited fiscal flexibility because of Labour’s election-winning manifesto commitments to not raise income tax, national insurance contributions or value-added tax.
It makes finance minister John Healey’s first budget on October 28 a difficult one.
Burnham told interviewers Friday that he would not call an early election before the required date of August 2029 to remove those red lines.
“All of this speculation on an early election, I can knock that dead,” he told ITV.
Burnham said he wanted to focus on helping the public feel “a bit of hope in their lives again” and would use Tuesday’s speech to “say further about the direction I want to take the country”.

A YouGov poll published Thursday put support for Labour at 24 per cent and Reform on 22 per cent, a dramatic turnaround from last year when Nigel Farage’s anti-immigrant group enjoyed double-digit leads.
If an election were held tomorrow, Labour would lose its majority but would likely be able to lead a progressive coalition, the survey suggested.
“There’s still an underlying anxiety about how long ... (Labour’s) bounce will last given the very tricky fiscal situation the government is in,” political scientist Tim Bale told AFP.
“And the fact that Labour is still a long way off the 30 per cent or so that’s the minimum needed to ... win an election.” — AFP

bd3623e929727d18: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) Sabah has questioned the federal government’s transport infrastructure priorities, highlighting more than RM21 billion in approved transport projects in Penang while Sabah continues to face road maintenance needs and delays involving the Pan Borneo Highway.
Its Information Chief Mustaman Mustain said the federal government should clarify its priorities, particularly given Sabah’s extensive road network and infrastructure needs.
“Sabah is not asking for special treatment. Sabah is demanding development justice,” he said in a statement.

Citing a Sept 21 report by Sinar Harian, Mustaman said more than RM21 billion in transport projects in Penang had received Federal Government approval, including the RM16.8 billion Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) project, RM1.55 billion expansion of Penang International Airport, RM2.2 billion for Penang Port and RM500 million for Swettenham Pier.
He said PAS Sabah did not dispute Penang’s right to development, but questioned why Sabahans continued to face concerns over basic transport infrastructure.
Mustaman said the federal government allocated RM341.7 million for federal road maintenance in Sabah in 2025, covering about 1,536.949km of federal roads under its maintenance jurisdiction.

For 2026, he noted that RM200 million had been allocated for 178 federal road maintenance works in Sabah, comprising 74 periodic pavement works and 104 non-pavement works. The allocation represents a substantial increase from the RM50 million provided for the programme in 2025.

“Although this amount has increased from RM50 million in 2025, the question remains whether the allocation is sufficient to meet the actual needs of a state with an extensive road network, challenging terrain and dispersed population,” he said.
On the Pan Borneo Highway, Mustaman said RM1.67 billion had been allocated in 2026 to support the Sabah project, but Sabahans were still waiting for its full completion.

He said the effectiveness of infrastructure development should ultimately be assessed by outcomes, including the number of roads repaired, projects completed and the time taken to deliver safe and comprehensive transport infrastructure.
“Sabah must be regarded as a partner in the Federation that is entitled to infrastructure development commensurate with its contribution and position within the country,” he said.

Mustaman also called on the federal government to translate its Malaysia Madani and development-gap reduction agenda into tangible outcomes, saying Sabahans wanted to see concrete results. — The Borneo Post
4db551648c185098: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — Authorities have been urged to clarify tourist safety measures, land status and regulatory oversight at Mengalum Island following the death of a Chinese tourist during a snorkelling activity on Sept 23.

Warisan vice-president Datuk Junz Wong said the police investigation should be allowed to take its course, but the incident also raised broader questions over how tourism activities at the island were monitored and regulated.

He said tourist safety should not rest with a single agency, calling for clearer coordination among Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK), the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department, Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Environment Sabah (KePKAS), Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture Malaysia (Motac) and other relevant agencies.
“The issue is not only whether the boat operator and vessel were properly licensed.

“We must also ask whether the tourism activities and facilities at the destination itself have the necessary approvals and whether the relevant safety procedures were properly implemented,” he said in a statement.
Junz also called on DBKK to clarify its procedures for operators using its public jetty, including whether licences and approvals were verified before tourists were transported to the island.
He said any gaps between the responsibilities of the various agencies must be identified and addressed, while calling for a comprehensive inspection of operators serving Mengalum Island.
“Preventive enforcement is needed rather than action only after an incident occurred,” he said.
Meanwhile, Luyang assemblyman Samuel Wong said the status of land and tourism facilities at Mengalum should be clarified separately from the police investigation.
“To be clear, we are not saying that the land status or TOL was the cause of the tourist’s death. There must be evidence before any such connection can be made,” he said.
However, he said authorities should establish whether the land, structures, jetties and tourism facilities used by operators had the necessary approvals.

Samuel urged the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department to clarify the status of any Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) and land occupation, while KePKAS and Motac should clarify the licensing and safety requirements applicable to the operator.

He said authorities should also determine whether tourists were given proper safety briefings, adequate safety equipment was provided and sufficient trained personnel were present to monitor the snorkelling activity and respond to emergencies.
Junz and Samuel also called for previous safety incidents at Mengalum to be reviewed to identify any recurring weaknesses.
“The death of a tourist is deeply saddening. We respect the police investigation and will not prejudge the outcome.

“But the incident must also prompt a serious review of the existing tourism safety and enforcement system. Every agency must understand and carry out its responsibility, and any regulatory or safety gaps must be addressed before another tragedy occurs,” they said. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: DBKK is the abbreviation for Dewan Bandaraya Kota Kinabalu, or Kota Kinabalu City Hall, while KePKAS is the abbreviation for the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Environment Sabah.
0aa17a6500a5aabb: KUCHING, Sept 27 — Putrajaya must first work out the one-third formula for Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat before adding any parliamentary seats.

Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said she and several Sarawak leaders, including in Cabinet, have raised the issue, but the focus had previously been more on state assembly seats.

“Speaking on voicing out in terms of (Parliamentary) seats, I am with Yang Berhormat Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi in Cabinet. How that one-third formula is to be created needs to be discussed together, in terms of legislation,” she said.
She said further discussions to determine a suitable method and measure must be held between the Sarawak premier, Sabah chief minister and the Federal Government.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed in principle to increase the ratio of Sabah and Sarawak representation in the Dewan Rakyat, in line with the regions’ position in the formation of Malaysia through the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
He said the decision was among the key matters agreed at the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting.

Meanwhile, former Sabah Chief Minister Salleh Said Keruak called on Putrajaya to clarify how many additional parliamentary seats it intends to allocate to Sabah and Sarawak, and whether it is committed to one-third representation for the two states.

“More seats do not necessarily strengthen Sabah and Sarawak if seats in Peninsular Malaysia also increase and the overall ratio remains largely unchanged. The real issue, therefore, is not how many seats are added, but what proportion of parliamentary seats Sabah and Sarawak will ultimately hold,” he said.

Salleh, who is also the Sabah Umno treasurer, said the government should make clear whether its objective is to achieve one-third representation for Sabah and Sarawak or merely increase their number of seats. He noted that when Malaysia was formed in 1963, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore together held about one-third of the parliamentary seats.
Following Singapore’s departure in 1965, the question remained as to whether the “spirit and balance” behind Malaysia’s formation should still be reflected in Sabah and Sarawak’s representation.
“For Sabah and Sarawak, this is not simply about getting more seats. It is about whether their representation reflects the spirit and understanding upon which Malaysia was formed,” he said.
Earlier, the Election Commission denied a report claiming that there was a proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak by 15.
Based on the current 222 seats in Parliament, an additional 18 are required for Sabah and Sarawak to reach the one-third figure.

EC secretary Khairul Shahril Idrus said there are currently no proposals to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak, as claimed by the report, in connection with discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963.
He said only the seventh Sarawak state constituency review and redelineation proposal had been prepared, and that it was currently on public display from Sept 1 to 30. — Daily Express
2f76d216c0e6da6a: KUALA LUMPUR: Pengerusi Barisan Nasional, Zahid Hamidi meminta Menteri Besar, Ismail Lasim menghadap Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir dan Undang Yang Empat untuk mencari penyelesaian terhadap kemelut pentadbiran Negeri Sembilan.

Beliau turut meminta Ismail menghadap Tunku Besar Tampin, Datuk Shahbandar dan hierarki adat lain bagi mencari menyelesaikan kemelut itu dengan mengambil kira Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS), adat serta peraturan.
"Yang penting, rakyat mesti diberikan keutamaan. Masalah mereka mesti ditangani dan disantuni dan apa yang sedang berlaku dan telah berlaku, kita cari jalan penyelesaian baik di peringkat negeri.

"Tentunya kita tidak mahu keadaan semakin keruh dan rakyat dimangsakan dengan situasi ini," katanya selepas merasmikan Mesyuarat Agung Tahunan ke-18 Parti Makkal Sakti di Pusat Dagangan Dunia Kuala Lumpur.
Timbalan perdana menteri itu berkata, keutamaan ketika ini ialah memastikan kepentingan rakyat terus terpelihara dan pentadbiran negeri berjalan lancar selepas pemecatan 10 exco.
Menurutnya, beliau akan menemui 25 Adun BN dan Perikatan Nasional di ibu pejabat Umno malam ini bagi membincangkan pilihan untuk menyelesaikan kemelut itu.

"Keseluruhan 25 Adun yang ada, yang telah membentuk lebih tiga perempat kerajaan di Negeri Sembilan ini...dua pertiga daripada mandat yang telah diberikan ini mesti terus diberikan keutamaan dan penyelesaiannya akan datang daripada mereka.

"Saya mahu dengar apakah pilihan terbaik bagi kita menyelesaikan masalah sedang melanda Negeri Sembilan," katanya sambil menegaskan beliau tidak berniat campur tangan urusan pentadbiran negeri, sebaliknya mahu menyelaras perbincangan bagi mencari jalan penyelesaian terbaik.
Beliau turut menolak cadangan darurat diisytiharkan di Negeri Sembilan susulan kemelut berkenaan.

"Saya tidak fikir ia harus menuju ke arah itu sebab tidak ada sebarang kekecohan dari segi keamanan di Negeri Sembilan dan tak perlu pun perkara itu difikirkan. Tentu ada pilihan lebih baik selain mengisytiharkan darurat dan menubuhkan Emergency Council di Negeri Sembilan."
Sementara itu, Zahid menafikan dakwaan 10 bekas exco Negeri Sembilan telah dipanggil Bukit Aman, sebaliknya memaklumkan mereka bersedia memberikan keterangan, jika diperlukan.

"Perkara itu tidak benar dan tidak ada keperluan untuk dipanggil. Tetapi, kalau Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia mahu mendapat keterangan, tentunya exco atau mantan exco tidak ada masalah memberi keterangan di Seremban atau mana-mana tempat di Negeri Sembilan."
PRN Melaka: BN terbuka bincang keperluan PAS guna logo BN
Zahid berkata, BN akan berbincang dengan pihak berkaitan, termasuk keperluan PAS menggunakan logo BN pada PRN Melaka susulan penggantungan PN oleh Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan.
"Pada minggu ini, kita akan ada perbincangan dengan beberapa pihak, dengan parti gabungan mana, dengan parti mana kita akan bertanding.
"Kita menghormati keputusan yang akan dibuat oleh mereka. Logo dan lambang apa yang akan mereka gunakan, itu terserah kepada mereka."

Dalam perkembangan lain, Zahid berkata, tabung membantu Najib Razak mencecah RM9.25 juta setakat 10 pagi tadi, jauh daripada sasaran denda RM50 juta yang perlu dibayar untuk membolehkan bekas perdana menteri itu menjalani baki hukuman penjaranya di bawah tahanan rumah.
02d019e548540efd: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has asked Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Ismail Lasim to seek an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and the four undangs to resolve the state's ongoing crisis.

2a492cec16a54874: BANGKOK, Sept 27 — Flooding in Bangkok is showing signs of easing as rainfall subsides after a monsoon trough and low-pressure system moved away from the Thai capital.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said rainfall had eased compared with the past two to three days, with most areas now experiencing light to moderate rain.
The low-pressure system had moved towards western Thailand and Myanmar, while heavy rain had shifted to western parts of the country, he said.

“Rainfall conditions in Bangkok and the eastern region are showing an easing trend, becoming less severe compared with the past two to three days,” he said after visiting the Flood Prevention Centre of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) today.
A woman walks through flood waters in front of a bus after heavy rain in Bangkok on September 26, 2026. — AFP pic

Chadchart said water levels in canals near the Chao Phraya River had begun to recede, although several major canals, including Khlong Prem Prachakon, Khlong Lat Phrao, Khlong Saen Saep and Khlong Prawet Buri Rom, remained at critical levels.
“Pumping operations are continuing as water continues to flow into the canals from surrounding areas,” he said.
Chadchart advised residents to check road conditions before travelling, while response teams had been deployed to assist those stranded by flooding in Lat Krabang, Nong Chok and Min Buri.
Meanwhile, Deputy Government Spokesperson Ploythalay Laksameesaengchan said supplies of consumer goods and daily essentials remained sufficient and urged people not to panic.
She said the government was closely monitoring the flood situation and had instructed relevant agencies to coordinate efforts to assist affected communities.
“Inspections by the Department of Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce, confirm that supplies of consumer goods remain adequate, with no underlying factors warranting price increases,” she said.

The department had coordinated with manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers and convenience stores to monitor inventories, increase restocking and expedite distribution to areas experiencing high demand, noting that flooding had affected transportation and access to some outlets, she said. — Bernama
8327aa27a645d43c: PETALING JAYA: Inspector-General of Police Khalid Ismail has confirmed that the 10 former members of the Negeri Sembilan executive council will be summoned to assist in an investigation into the state's ongoing royal and administrative crisis.
Khalid said they will be summoned to give their statements from tomorrow, adding that multiple police reports have been lodged over the issue.
He said the statements of several other parties will also be taken to complete the investigation, Bernama reported.
"Many police reports have been filed by certain parties. We will investigate and record the statements of all involved, including the former exco members," he said.
Khalid refrained from disclosing any details on the investigation but did not dismiss the possibility of classifying the case under the Sedition Act.
Yesterday, a source told FMT that the 10 sacked Negeri Sembilan executive councillors will be questioned by federal police in Seremban.
Last Sunday, the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, revoked the appointments of the 10 exco members.
The palace said the exco members were found to have breached their oaths of office and pledge of allegiance to the state ruler, which they took on Aug 7.
The revocation of the appointments came a week after the exco released a joint statement purportedly affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as the state ruler.

On Friday, Wawasan chairman and former Senate president Rais Yatim pleaded not guilty after he was charged with sedition in connection with the purported proclamation of a new Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar.
5da8b4135e4ad1b5: AICHI, Sept 27 — Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani reportedly fell in straight games to China’s Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang in the Asian Games quarter-finals today, missing out on a men’s doubles medal.
According to Berita Harian, the world No. 6 Malaysians went down 13-21, 17-21 to the Paris 2024 Olympic silver medallists at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.
Their defeat ended Malaysia’s challenge in the men’s doubles after Aaron Chia-Tee Kai Wun were knocked out in the second round by South Korea’s Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae yesterday.

f3249d6e4b50a3ed: BUTTERWORTH: Polis akan memanggil bekas exco Negeri Sembilan mulai esok dan lusa untuk merekodkan keterangan bagi membantu siasatan ekoran kemelut pentadbiran dan institusi diraja Negeri Sembilan susulan beberapa laporan polis yang dibuat berhubung isu berkenaan.
Ketua Polis Negara, Khalid Ismail, berkata selain bekas exco, pihaknya turut akan mengambil keterangan daripada beberapa saksi dan individu lain yang berkaitan bagi melengkapkan siasatan kes.

"Memang banyak laporan polis telah dibuat oleh pihak-pihak tertentu (berhubung perkara itu), kita akan menjalankan siasatan dan mengambil keterangan daripada mereka yang berkaitan, termasuk bekas exco dan mereka yang terlibat.

"Setakat ini polis telah memanggil beberapa individu untuk dirakam percakapan, termasuk seorang atau dua individu yang berkemungkinan menjadi saksi dalam kes berkenaan," katanya kepada pemberita di sini hari ini.

Beliau ditemui selepas merasmikan Majlis Peluncuran Projek Whitening the Blackspot Kontinjen Polis Pulau Pinang di Pusat Konvensyen PICCA@Arena Butterworth, di sini. Yang turut hadir ialah Pengarah Jabatan Pencegahan Jenayah dan Keselamatan Komuniti Bukit Aman Noor Hisam Nordin serta Ketua Polis Pulau Pinang Dennis Lim Kwang Keng.
Mengulas lanjut, Khalid berkata pihaknya juga akan melengkapkan kertas siasatan dan sebelum dikemukakan kepada Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) untuk tindakan selanjutnya.

Ditanya mengenai peruntukan undang-undang yang digunakan dalam siasatan itu, beliau berkata polis masih meneliti secara menyeluruh kesemua laporan yang diterima, dan tidak menolak kemungkinan terdapat kes yang melibatkan Akta Hasutan atau peruntukan undang-undang lain.

"Polis menyiasat (tetapi) yang membuat keputusan sama ada hendak mendakwa dan sebagainya ialah peguam negara, mungkin dalam beberapa (kes) ada berkaitan dengan Akta Hasutan, mungkin ada pelanggaran lain dan memerlukan penelitian daripada semua pihak, terutama sekali pihak Jabatan Peguam Negara AG Chambers," katanya.

Dalam pada itu, Khalid berkata situasi keselamatan dan ketenteraman awam di Negeri Sembilan ketika ini berada dalam keadaan baik dan terkawal, serta masyarakat negeri itu dilihat memahami perkembangan semasa serta memberikan kerjasama yang baik kepada pihak berkuasa.
" … kita cuba mengekalkan suasana itu dengan sempurna demi keselamatan masyarakat dan juga rakyat di Negeri Sembilan," katanya.

936c6d32540441bf: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The police will summon former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members starting tomorrow and the day after to record their statements, to assist the investigation into the administrative and royal institution crisis in the state following several police reports lodged regarding the matter.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said in addition to the Exco members, the police would also take statements from several witnesses and other relevant individuals to complete the investigation.

“Indeed, numerous police reports have been lodged by certain parties (regarding the matter), so we will take action to conduct an investigation and subsequently record statements from relevant individuals, including former Exco members and those involved.

“Thus far, the police have summoned several individuals to have their statements recorded, including one or two individuals who may serve as witnesses in the case,” he said when met by reporters here today.

He said after officiating the launch of the Penang Police Contingent’s ‘Whitening the Blackspot’ project at Picca@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre here which was also attended by Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin and Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng.

Mohd Khalid made these remarks when asked to comment on the police investigation into the administrative and royal institution crisis in Negeri Sembilan from various angles, following several police reports lodged regarding the issue.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail was reported as saying that the police are focusing on preventing any acts of violence and ensuring public safety and order are maintained.
Elaborating further, Mohd Khalid said his team is also finalising the investigation papers, which will subsequently be submitted to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) for further action.

When asked about the legal provisions being applied in the investigation, he said the police are still comprehensively reviewing all reports received and do not rule out the possibility of cases involving the Sedition Act or other legal provisions.

“The police conduct the investigation while the party that decides whether to prosecute or otherwise is the Attorney General. Perhaps in some (cases) there may be links to the Sedition Act, or perhaps in.... other violations, and this requires scrutiny by all parties, especially the Attorney General’s Chambers,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mohd Khalid stated that the security and public order situation in Negeri Sembilan is currently stable and under control and the community appears to understand the current developments and is extending good cooperation to the authorities.

“Alhamdulillah, everything is fine and under control, it seems the community understands the situation and is providing excellent cooperation. We are striving to maintain this state of affairs for the safety of the community and the people of Negeri Sembilan,” he said. — Bernama
b438a4462aa4701d: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Artists can play an important role in ensuring that the Palestinian issue remains in the global spotlight by using their influence and platforms to speak out about the reality on the ground.

Palestinian academician and poet Dr Nida Younis said developments involving American rapper Macklemore following his stance on Palestine demonstrated how the actions of a single artist could trigger a much wider response from the international community.
She described the phenomenon as the “Macklemore effect,” likening it to the butterfly effect in which a single action can set off a much larger, far-reaching response.

“It is about courage. It is about standing for human rights and dignity. It is also about telling the whole world that silence is no longer an option,” she said during a recent interview on Bernama TV’s Bernama World programme titled Palestine Beyond The Headlines: Global Solidarity Through Art and Music.

Nida said Macklemore turned the concert stage into a platform to deliver a humanitarian message through his call of “Free Palestine,” sparking a wave of support for Palestine that extended beyond the borders of the United States (US).

She said the controversy following Macklemore’s removal from the remaining US tour dates had also brought greater attention to the Palestinian issue, as other artists and members of the public came forward to express their solidarity.

“Palestine is still remembered. Palestine is not forgotten, and Palestine continues to live in the hearts and minds of people around the world. Everyone is seeing what is happening in Gaza,” she said.

She said artists should not stop speaking out about Palestine and other humanitarian issues. They should convey what they witness and not allow others to dictate narratives that contradict the realities they see.

Nida also recalled British actress and Oscar winner Vanessa Redgrave’s support for Palestine in the 1970s, including financing the documentary The Palestinian, despite facing criticism and losing several career opportunities because of her stance.
She said art in its various forms such as music, film, poetry, and literature, has the power to convey humanitarian messages to people around the world.
“When politics and the media fail, poetry, art, and culture will rise and play their role,” she said. — Bernama
6fb2e0b565c76871: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) is keeping a round-the-clock watch on earthquake activity in Sabah via 28 seismic stations statewide.
MET Malaysia director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the monitoring enables the department to detect and analyse earthquakes swiftly.

He said the seismic stations closest to the epicentre are Sapulut, 57.23 kilometres away; Keningau (66.51 kilometres); Sandakan/Telupid (74.36 kilometres); Matupang (76.67 kilometres); and Tenom (93.32 kilometres).

“Quake information will be disseminated within six minutes of detection, subject to data availability. To date, there is still no technology capable of predicting earthquakes,” he said in a statement today.
The statement follows a weak magnitude 3.3 earthquake that struck Kuamut, Kinabatangan, at 5.32 am yesterday.
Mohd Hisham said earthquakes cannot be predicted in terms of time, location or magnitude, and seismic stations only serve to detect and determine a quake’s magnitude after the event.
He said tsunami threats, meanwhile, can be assessed based on earthquake magnitude and related monitoring data.
“If there is a potential tsunami threat, MET Malaysia will issue the relevant information and warnings,” he said.
He said installing additional seismic stations or sensors at a given location can strengthen local monitoring coverage and capability, but this does not mean earthquakes can be predicted earlier.
“MET Malaysia will continue to monitor seismic activity in Sabah and channel fast, accurate and verified information to the public and relevant agencies,” he said.
In light of this, the public is advised to obtain information on earthquakes and tsunamis only through MET Malaysia’s official channels. — Bernama
767e7d11f0a3d235: TEHRAN, Sept 27 — Iran stood firm today on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite US President Donald Trump’s rejection of the proposal that had created some optimism for breaking the Mideast war stalemate.
The waterway is key to the world’s energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.

Iran’s plan called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and fulfilling conditions in the ceasefire deal that fell apart months ago.
That agreement, which dissolved during fighting over Hormuz, called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade.

“Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being fulfilled. We will not back down from them,” Araghchi said today, state broadcaster IRIB reported.
“We have never closed the door to diplomacy or negotiations, but at the same time, we have never backed down from our rights.”
But Trump said yesterday that he rejected the truce deal.
“They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” he told reporters. “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I like making a deal too.”
Araghchi said today that the Iranians “saw the first reaction from the US president, but so far, nothing has been conveyed to us by the mediators”.
“We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive positions to us, and we will make a decision based on them,” the foreign minister added.
‘Tool for pressure’
Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, to reopen the strait and to launch talks on Iran’s nuclear programme.
But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.
Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.
Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the US sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

At the UN, Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan complained that the “international community has been absent” and is failing to live up to the responsibility to keep the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab open.

“The kingdom rejects any party’s use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states,” he said, stressing the waterways’ importance to global energy security.

His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, told member states that “Russia, together with other responsible states, stands ready to constructively contribute to stabilising this strategically important region.”

In New York, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to his office, and said: “Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table but, given past experiences, it no longer trusts the US.”

Araghchi said at the UN: “Iran has conveyed to the US, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days.”
“The choice now rests with the US. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure,” he added.
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: “We will not cease punishing the US until Iran’s seven conditions are met.”
Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands. — AFP
2deec9b0114c33df: PUTRAJAYA: The families of 55 Malaysians still missing following a glacial flash flood disaster in Nepal on Aug 26 are seeking clarity on the search for their loved ones as the wait enters day 33.

S Punitha, aunt of missing Suguna Balan, 33, said the families were not only grappling with uncertainty over the fate of their loved ones but also feeling the financial and emotional toll of the ordeal.
She said Suguna was the main breadwinner for her family, which now needs clear information on what to do next.
“We hope we can get solid information about what happened and what steps we need to take. It has been 33 days, but we still have no news about the 55 missing people.
"We have not even been told whether their belongings, such as luggage or personal items, have been found,” she told reporters at Wisma Putra here today.
Punitha was among family members who came to the foreign ministry's headquarters, Wisma Putra, here to get an update on the latest development concerning the missing Malaysians.
She said Suguna’s parents - Punitha's elder sister and brother-in-law - were still traumatised by the loss of their daughter and struggling to come to terms with what had happened.
Another next of kin, M Subramaniam, 38, the son-in-law of V Krishnan, 74, said the family still hoped those missing might have survived or were in locations yet to be identified.

“Today is the 33rd day. All the families are desperate for answers, and we still do not know whether they are alive or not. We are still holding out hope that there will be news that they are safe or perhaps stranded at some camp," he said.
He added that among the main issues the families wanted clarified was the progress of the search on both sides of the Nepal-China border, as well as updates from the relevant authorities.
Subramanian said the families also wanted to know whether the group of Malaysians had managed to cross the Tibet immigration checkpoint before the disaster struck.
He claimed his father-in-law and 26 others were last known to be inside a building, and that the information on the location had been conveyed to Wisma Putra.
Today’s closed-door meeting was the second engagement between the foreign ministry and the families following the disaster on Aug 26.

The Aug 26 floods and debris flow, triggered by an ice and rock collapse in the upper catchment of Lhende Khola in Tibet, reportedly killed more than 1,450 people, while thousands more remain unaccounted for.
0ae5b2fbf72e2cdc: KUALA LUMPUR: Gangguan sistem semboyan di antara Kalumpang dan Kuala Kubu Bharu semalam menyebabkan perkhidmatan KTM Komuter dan ETS mengalami kelewatan hingga lima jam.

Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) dalam kenyataan hari ini menyebut kelewatan tertinggi bagi KTM Komuter melibatkan tren No 2389 selama 230 minit, manakala bagi perkhidmatan ETS, EP9138 (KL Sentral-Butterworth) merekodkan kelewatan 305 minit.

Menurut KTMB, pemeriksaan awal mendapati gangguan berpunca daripada kerosakan pada satu daripada komponen sistem yang menyebabkan percikan dan seterusnya menjejaskan sistem semboyan, namun punca kerosakan komponen berkenaan masih dalam siasatan lanjut.

“Gangguan sistem semboyan tersebut telah memberikan kesan berantai kepada pergerakan dan jadual perjalanan tren lain yang melalui sektor berkenaan, khususnya perkhidmatan dari dan ke arah utara,” menurut kenyataan itu.

Pada masa sama, KTMB memaklumkan kerja-kerja menaik taraf Landasan Berkembar Rawang-Ipoh yang telah dijadualkan lebih awal turut dilaksanakan secara berperingkat, termasuk di laluan Kalumpang pada semalam dan hari ini, sekali gus melibatkan penyelarasan jadual perkhidmatan di laluan berkenaan.

“Susulan gangguan sistem semboyan yang berlaku ketika kerja-kerja tersebut sedang dilaksanakan, pergerakan tren menjadi lebih terhad dan seterusnya menyebabkan kesan kelewatan berganda kepada beberapa perkhidmatan KTM Komuter dan ETS,” menurut kenyataan itu.
Bagaimanapun, KTMB menyebut kerja-kerja pemulihan selesai pada 5.15 pagi tadi dan tren Komuter pertama dari Tanjung Malim telah berlepas pada 5.45 pagi tadi.

Menurut pengendali perkhidmatan pengangkutan rel negara itu, operasi perkhidmatan KTM Komuter dan ETS kini kembali seperti biasa, namun terdapat reaksi kelewatan 30 minit daripada jadual asal ekoran masalah kerosakan semboyan di laluan Batang kali.

Sehubungan itu, KTMB memohon maaf kepada para penumpang terjejas susulan kejadian itu, manakala pemulangan tambang penuh akan diberikan kepada mereka yang memilih untuk tidak meneruskan perjalanan berikutan gangguan tersebut, tertakluk kepada prosedur yang berkuat kuasa.
80db9e4632fb3fd5: ALMATY: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Dauren Kosanov as defence minister following the deaths of military personnel during exercises in the Caspian Sea, Tokayev’s office said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
“By decree of the head of state, Dauren Zhumataevich Kosanov has been relieved of his duties as Minister of Defence of the Republic of Kazakhstan,” the statement said.

On Thursday, the Kazakh defence ministry said that 17 naval personnel had been swept out to sea during exercises in the Mangystau region on the Caspian coast due to a sudden deterioration in weather conditions and strengthening winds.
Fourteen of them died, while three were rescued.
A criminal case has been opened into the deaths of the sailors on charges of “negligent performance of duty resulting in grave consequences” and “violation of navigation rules”.
A government commission was established to investigate the causes and circumstances of the tragedy.
The Kazakh interior ministry previously announced the detention of five defence ministry officials in connection with the investigation.
Tokayev ordered the creation of a commission to conduct a comprehensive audit of the agency and instructed it to present preliminary findings within seven days.
fddb93f9a6d26923: NEW YORK, Sept 27 — US aerospace giant Boeing has confirmed a technical glitch in the software of its 737 MAX aircraft that could cause problems with an automated navigation function, according to The Wall Street Journal yesterday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
The glitch has raised concerns about a potential safety risk when the aircraft is landing, the report said.
The issue emerged following an update to the cockpit software and could occur when the crew changes the planned flight path after a missed approach, it added.
The newspaper added that, in certain scenarios, pilots may have to fly the aircraft manually without some autopilot functions.
This could place excessive demands on pilots who are already busy flying at low altitude and may also be dealing with conditions such as bad weather. — Bernama-Sputnik/Ria Novosti
ae3df97c6ee41bd7: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 27 — ChatGPT developer OpenAI has paused work involving its most capable artificial intelligence models after one of its systems bypassed internet restrictions and contacted an external chatbot during a test, German news agency dpa reported.
The model was not supposed to have internet access but found and exploited a gap in the test environment’s network controls caused by insufficient DNS filtering, OpenAI said in a blog post.
Training, evaluation and inference involving tool use are to remain paused until the company is confident the gap has been closed and further safety testing has been carried out.
OpenAI said the incident was less serious than some previous cases but was the first since safeguards were tightened following an earlier hacking incident involving AI platform Hugging Face.

During the test, the model was asked to identify a person who had written a blog post using a series of clues. After failing to find the answer in a simulated web environment, it discovered it could use the system’s DNS resolver to send queries to a chatbot on the open internet.
OpenAI stopped the test after detecting the communication.
The incident follows several other cases involving OpenAI systems.
In one, AI software placed 53 images uploaded by users on online platforms. OpenAI said the links were not public and most of the images had since been removed.
OpenAI agents have also interacted unexpectedly with several US government websites, including accessing or copying publicly available information.
The company said it had notified “dozens” of organisations whose websites had been interacted with in unintended ways by its software.
The most high-profile case so far involved an OpenAI system breaking out of a secured test environment and gaining unintended access to computers belonging to Hugging Face. — Bernama-dpa
3face5019fa9faf4: MEXICO CITY: Thousands of protesters wore red and carried symbolic coffins during a demonstration in Mexico City on Saturday, demanding answers about the 43 trainee teachers who went missing 12 years ago.

President Claudia Sheinbaum, who regularly meets with the disappeared's families, is expected to present a report Monday on the latest progress in the case, following an exhaustive review of the evidence by the attorney general's office.
"Because they were taken alive, we want them back alive," one banner slogan read.
The protest was led by parents of the 43 teacher trainees from Ayotzinapa, who led the procession to the capital's main square, where the government palace is located.
Others counted to 43 several times to honor each of the trainees from the rural teachers' college who disappeared on September 26, 2014.
"Another year of strain, of exhaustion, of hopelessness," Estanislao Mendoza, one of the parents of the 43, told AFP.
"We want to know, whether it's good or bad, alive or dead, but to know the truth, to know where they are," he said. "Twelve years of suffering, of lies."
The students were traveling from Guerrero state to a protest in Mexico City. Local police stopped them in the town of Iguala, where six died in an hours-long street clash and 43 later went missing.
Prosecutors initially said the officers delivered the 43 teacher trainees to drug cartel hitmen, who killed them, incinerated their bodies and dumped the remains in a river.
However, independent human rights experts have rejected the government's conclusion, and the unsolved case remains a stain on Mexico's reputation.
A former governor was arrested in August, on accusations of deleting the security videos of the scene of the crime in Iguala. The former state attorney general was also arrested in 2022.
More than 134,000 people are listed as disappeared in Mexico.

"It's necessary to support a struggle against the indifference of a government that refuses to accept that there is a disappearance crisis," said 69-year-old Atanacio Pina, whose missing son was later found dead.
82376adcea80ccdd: DUNGUN: Bekas mudir sebuah maahad tahfiz di daerah ini direman lima hari bagi membantu siasatan dakwaan amang seksual tiga pelajar lelaki berusia 13 dan 14 tahun dari April hingga September 2025.
Ketua Polis Dungun, Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat, berkata perintah reman mulai hari ini sehingga Khamis itu dikeluarkan Majistret Ng Yan Ni selepas membenarkan permohonan polis di Mahkamah Majistret Dungun.
Beliau berkata, permohonan reman itu bagi membolehkan siasatan mengikut Seksyen 14(b) dan 14(d) Akta Kesalahan-kesalahan Seksual terhadap Kanak-kanak 2017 dijalankan.
Menurutnya, lelaki berusia 26 tahun itu yang kini guru sambilan hafazan di sebuah sekolah agama di daerah itu ditahan di kediamannya di Paka kira-kira 11 malam tadi.
"Polis menerima tiga laporan berhubung kejadian itu semalam dan siasatan awal mendapati ketiga-tiga mangsa merupakan bekas pelajar maahad berkenaan pada 2025."
9484df96aab7b480: BANGKOK: Thousands of Bangkok residents awoke in shelters on Sunday after flooding triggered by days of heavy rain in the Thai capital inundated homes and roads, with some starting to dry out their homes and belongings.

Nearly 4,900 people have been evacuated to shelters, with around 52,000 households affected by the floods, which prompted a disaster declaration across the capital, according to the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA).
More than 330 millimetres of rain fell in some areas of the city between Thursday and Sunday, the weather agency said.
Thailand is used to wet weather and September is the peak of the rainy season, but several Bangkok residents said this year seemed worse.
"Our house was underwater for about 30 hours," office worker Kosin Nilset, who lives along the Premprachakorn canal on the outskirts of the capital, told AFP on Sunday morning.
"This time, the water level is higher than the 2011 flood," the 44-year-old said.
Widespread deluges across the Southeast Asian country in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.
Kosin and his family lifted their belongings once they saw the water level was higher than the canal retaining wall, but their ground floor was still left soaked.
"At least tap water and electricity are working," Kosin said, as he used a broom to sweep out water.

Pedestrians in plastic rain ponchos trudged through murky floodwaters in Bangkok's east -- knee-deep in some areas of a grocery store parking lot -- floating their belongings in plastic tubs alongside them, AFP journalists saw.
'Sleeping on the table'
Water levels in Bangkok's network of canals remained high on Sunday morning, with authorities working to speed up drainage, the BMA said.
More rain was forecast throughout Sunday for Bangkok and its surrounding provinces, but would begin to taper off on Monday, it said.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events will increase as the planet continues to heat up because of fossil fuel emissions.
Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt said several roads were still flooded and warned Bangkok residents in a Facebook Live post to avoid unnecessary travel.
Chadchart visited a temporary shelter on Saturday night in a school in the Kheha Romklao area, where he said about 1,000 people were evacuated.
Some rested on cots and benches with their dogs in hallways, while others lay with blankets on the floors of classrooms where desks and chairs were pushed to the side.
Hundreds of city schools will be closed on Monday, according to the BMA.
Some convenience stores had empty shelves over the weekend as residents raced to buy essentials.
The prime minister's office asked the public to avoid panic-buying and warned that price gouging was a criminal offence.
Thidarat Silsuwan, 56, lives alone in her partially submerged house along the Premprachakorn canal.
"I have been sleeping on the table for two days now," she told AFP.
She did not want to go to a shelter as she worked to clean up and salvage her belongings.
"I tried to lift everything up, but I gave up on large electric appliances like the refrigerator and washing machine. I guess they are broken."

d8af0d48b85e85b9: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu Melaka sedia menggunakan lambang sendiri pada PRN akan datang jika Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan (JPPM) terus menggantung Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Ketua Penerangan Bersatu Melaka, Hishamuddin Abdul Karim, bagaimanapun berkata keputusan muktamad tertakluk kepada pertimbangan kepimpinan tertinggi parti.

"Ia mengambil kira perkembangan semasa serta bentuk kerjasama politik yang mungkin dipersetujui," katanya kepada FMT sambil memaklumkan Bersatu menggunakan lambang sendiri pada PRN Negeri Sembilan Ogos lalu.
Beliau berkata, jentera Bersatu Melaka tetap bergerak dan persiapan menghadapi PRN tidak bergantung kepada persoalan lambang semata-mata.
JPPM menggantung PN Rabu lalu selepas mengeluarkan notis kepada gabungan itu untuk menjelaskan aduan dikemukakan Bersatu.
JPPM berkata, penggantungan itu bertujuan menjaga kepentingan PN daripada terus melanggar peraturan.
Hishamuddin mengesahkan perbincangan kerjasama politik dengan Pakatan Harapan (PH) sedang berlangsung di peringkat negeri dan pusat.

Katanya, Bersatu Melaka terbuka mempertimbangkan sebarang bentuk kerjasama politik yang mungkin dijalin bagi menghadapi PRN, termasuk cadangan atau kerangka "PH Plus" yang pernah dimaklumkan secara terbuka oleh Pengerusi PH Melaka, Adly Zahari.

"Apa juga bentuk kerjasama, formula pembahagian kerusi atau pendekatan menghadapi PRN masih tertakluk sepenuhnya kepada pertimbangan, keputusan dan arahan kepimpinan parti," katanya sambil menambah belum ada keputusan muktamad dibuat, termasuk agihan kerusi.

82a96d71695c9c19: SYDNEY: The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, days after the revelation that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country's health-system database.
The Medicare breach, condemned by prime minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US.

OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesman for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe.
OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

The OpenAI agent's incursion on one of the country's most used government agencies may prompt Albanese's Labor government to toughen AI-specific laws it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra's ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say.
The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI.

"There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites," Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei "must front up, face the Senate's questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like", she said.
Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it "unacceptable", saying he had voiced "extreme concern" to Altman.

OpenAI says it only learned of the breach -- one of at least four of Australian government websites -- in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information.

Only 13.8% of people polled backed Anutin as prime minister in September, compared with 21.7% in June, according to a Sept 18-23 nationwide phone survey of 2,500 adults by the National Institute of Development Administration.

Anutin’s government faces its biggest political test yet on Monday, when the Constitutional Court is due to rule on a challenge to the validity of the February election that brought Bhumjaithai to power. The case centers on allegations that codes printed on ballot papers could have compromised voting secrecy.
If the court invalidates the election, Thailand could be required to hold a new vote.

The latest poll was held before severe flooding hit Bangkok, adding another challenge for the government. The capital declared all 50 districts disaster zones after nearly 300 millimeters of rain fell over about 48 hours, swamping major roads and disrupting businesses and transportation.

Opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut remained the most popular named choice for prime minister in the poll, although his support slipped to 24.7% from 26.1% in June. The share of respondents who couldn’t identify a suitable candidate nearly doubled to 19.8% from 10.2%.
Pheu Thai’s Yodchanan Wongsawat placed fourth overall with 11.3%, little changed from 11.6% in the previous survey, while former prime minister Abhisit Vejjajiva’s support fell to 9.60% from 11.8%.
The People’s Party retained a commanding lead in party preferences, edging up to 35.4% from 34.8%. Pheu Thai rose to 18.4% from 16.8%, while the Democrat Party declined to 9.8% from 12.7%.

773569ac081723f3: From Wan Agyl Wan Hassan
Malaysia does not lack road safety standards. We have engineering manuals, design guidelines, Road Safety Audits and experienced professionals across government.
But does every Malaysian receive the same minimum level of road-safety protection, regardless of who manages the road?

A motorcyclist does not become less vulnerable when moving from a federal road onto a state road. A parent taking a child to school should not need to know whether the road outside the school belongs to the public works department (JKR), the state or a local council.
An elderly person trying to reach a bus stop does not know which authority manages the crossing in front of them.
For road users, it is simply our road system.

Yet our roads are planned, designed and maintained by different levels of government. Federal roads, state roads, expressways and local authority roads have different functions, responsibilities and funding arrangements.

There are good reasons for these differences. An expressway should not be designed like a residential street. A rural road has different needs from a busy town centre. A kampung road cannot simply follow the same design as an urban arterial in Kuala Lumpur.
I'm not suggesting that every Malaysian road should look the same, but asking whether every road should meet an agreed minimum safety level.

Malaysia has already set the direction through the Malaysia Road Safety Plan 2022–2030, which targets a 50% reduction in road deaths by 2030 and identifies safer infrastructure as one of its priority areas.
The ambition is clear. The challenge is making sure the entire system helps deliver it.
When a serious crash happens, we question if the driver was speeding, whether the motorcyclist was careless or whether enforcement was adequate.
But they should not be the only questions.

Was the road designed for the speed vehicles actually travel? Could people cross safely? Were motorcyclists properly considered? Was the junction designed to reduce dangerous conflicts? Was the road properly maintained? Had development around the road changed how people were using it?
And when someone makes an ordinary human mistake, does the road environment help prevent that mistake from becoming a death or serious injury?
That is the thinking behind the Safe System approach. People will make mistakes. Our roads should be designed so that those mistakes do not routinely become fatal.

This is particularly important in Malaysia because motorcycles are part of everyday mobility. Any road-safety framework that does not consider motorcyclists from the onset will struggle to reflect the reality of our roads.
The same applies to pedestrians, children, older people, persons with disabilities, cyclists and people walking to and from public transport.
Road safety cannot therefore be measured only by how efficiently vehicles move. It must also consider how safely someone can ride to work, walk to school, cross a road or reach a bus stop.

We found that Malaysia's challenge is not the absence of technical guidance. We already have substantial engineering and planning standards. The question is whether their application across federal, state and local roads ultimately provides a common minimum level of protection.
We're not saying our existing system has failed. It is about strengthening what we already have.
JKR's own Road Safety Audit guidance recognises the importance of greater consistency in how safety audits are managed and implemented across different authorities.
Our road environments are also changing.

A road originally built mainly to move traffic may eventually be surrounded by houses, shops, schools, factories and bus stops. More people start walking and crossing. More vehicles enter and leave roadside premises. Motorcycle movements increase.
The road may carry the same classification, but the way people use it has changed. Our approach to safety must be able to respond to that change.
This is why Malaysia should begin discussing a common national road-safety floor.
The principle is simple. Different roads. Different functions. Different local contexts. One minimum level of safety.
A school zone should provide an agreed minimum level of protection whether it sits beside a federal, state or local road.

Pedestrian facilities should reflect the actual speed and risk of the road. Motorcycle safety should be considered in barriers, road surfaces, intersections and other conflict points. Road Safety Audits should identify serious risks and ensure they are properly addressed.
Roads should continue to be assessed as traffic, development and communities change.
This does not mean replacing existing JKR standards or taking decision-making away from states and local authorities. Neither should this become a federal exercise imposed on them.
A national safety floor must be developed together, recognising the responsibilities, expertise, local conditions and different implementation capacities of each level of government.

This matters because not every authority has the same resources. A large city council may have significant engineering capability. A smaller municipal or district council may face very different constraints.
If we agree on higher national expectations, we must also discuss technical support, capacity building, funding and realistic implementation.
That is why I do not believe we should begin with another directive, another manual or immediate legislation.
We should begin by getting everyone around the same table.

Malaysia should convene a National Roundtable on Safe Road and Street Standards, bringing together federal, state and local government, alongside our road engineers, planners, researchers, road-safety institutions and representatives of road users.
And it should start with one simple question: what minimum level of safety should no Malaysian road be allowed to fall below?
From there, we can examine what already works, where greater consistency is needed and where states and local authorities should retain flexibility.
We can also identify roads with the highest risks and progressively improve them.

Start with the areas where intervention can save the most lives. Test the approach across federal, state and local roads. Measure the results. Learn from them. Then determine what technical, regulatory or funding changes are actually necessary.
It should help us deliver the national road-safety ambition we have already committed to.
Malaysia already has capable institutions, engineers, planners and road-safety professionals. What we need now is to bring that expertise together around one common principle:
A Malaysian should not receive a different minimum level of road-safety protection simply because a road falls under a different jurisdiction.

Our roads may serve different purposes. They may be designed differently. They may be managed by different authorities. But the value of the person using them does not change at the jurisdictional boundary.
That is the conversation Malaysia should begin now. And getting federal, state and local government around the same table is the right place to start.
Wan Agyl Wan Hassan is the founder and senior adviser of MY Mobility Vision, a transport think tank.

24b763f23e794b8a: The mood on the ground in Malaysia is heavy with a deep, suffocating weariness. People are simply tired
They are tired of politics and the power plays that have dragged focus, energy and resources away from building the economy and addressing the rising cost of living.

They are tired of watching the federal unity government navigate its own fragile choreography—with Umno Youth rattling sabres about realignments with PAS, whispers of possible early polls and convicted former prime minister Najib Razak’s conditional royal pardon which allows for house arrest.

Adding to the turbulence, the Negeri Sembilan political landscape appears to be spinning into administrative chaos. What began as a move by several traditional chieftains (undang) to remove the ruler has become more entangled and ugly with the involvement of the menteri besar and state executive council in a high-stakes power play.
The people are exhausted by a system where political survival and power are chased for their own sake, while ordinary families bear the brunt of rising costs and uneven development.

Compounding this instability is something even more dangerous: a profound crisis of public trust. Malaysians have grown deeply cynical, widely viewing politicians as power-hungry actors looking out primarily for themselves.
How do we break out of this exhausting loop? Perhaps the answer lies not in inventing new political spin, but in turning back the clock to timeless wisdom.

Global leaders occasionally lean on ancient texts to remind modern states of foundational statecraft. This was brought sharply into focus when reports emerged of India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi presenting Russian President Vladimir Putin with a Russian translation of the ancient Thirukkural on the sidelines of the recent BRICS summit in New Delhi.
Having read the text, I could understand Modi's choice of cultural diplomacy—taking a 2,000-year-old masterpiece on governance, ethics, and human conduct and placing it on the global stage.

Modi frequently quotes from the Thirukkural, as does our own Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. For instance, in tabling the 2024 federal budget in October 2023, Anwar noted that according to the Thirukkural, a good ruler is one who is capable of creating wealth, acquiring it, protecting it, and distributing it wisely for the welfare of the people.
In 2025, in talking about the burdens of the rising cost of living in Parliament, Anwar reminded Malaysians of the text's lesson that steadfastness of the heart is a core mark of human virtue.

Long before modern party politics and coalition arithmetic, the ancient Tamil text—composed by Tiruvalluvar—laid down a remarkably clear framework for governance. Its core principles offer an unsparing mirror for today’s politicians if they care to look.

Early icons of independent Malaysia understood this resonance. First prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman heaped profuse praise upon the Thirukkural, as did national laureate Dr Ismail Hussein, who felt it held vital lessons for all of mankind.

Perhaps it’s time to introduce today’s politicians to this timeless wisdom, which transcends race, religion, and creed. We already possess distinguished Malay translations of the Tamil original, including works by Dr Ismail Hussein and Dr S Singaravelu, formerly of Universiti Malaya.

If our members of Parliament and state assemblymen genuinely imbibe these tenets, our public life could look entirely different, providing an ethical counterweight against systemic governance failures.
The Thirukkural rests on three essential pillars: aram (justice/virtue/righteousness), porul (material prosperity/politics/governance) and inbam (love/joy/human connection).

Aram deals with ethics, morality, and the leading of a balanced, honest life; porul focuses on the practicalities of governance, economics, and the social responsibilities of citizens and leaders; and inbam explores the nuances of intimacy, longing, and emotional connection.

The Thirukkural has many gems for both the ordinary citizen and rulers/leaders. For instance, it says good rulers/leaders are marked by courage, liberality, wisdom, energy, diligence and learning. They must also be easy of access and soft-spoken.

At the heart of the text with 1,330 couplets or Kural is a deep commitment to justice, the virtue that prevents resentment and division. Tiruvalluvar insists that true leaders must act with strict impartiality and safeguard the dignity of every single citizen.

In today's climate of fragile state-level realignments and casual ethnic grandstanding, this is more urgent than ever. Kural 317, for instance, states: "It is the highest wisdom not to cause pain to any living creature, at any time, in any degree, even in thought."

For our leaders, this is a practical warning against the abuse of power and divisive rhetoric that leaves communities feeling marginalised. Applying justice means defending an independent judiciary, maintaining fearless anti-corruption frameworks, and enacting policies rooted in equal opportunity rather than racial patronage.
Equally critical is the text’s emphasis on economic pragmatism and resource management, prioritising public welfare over elite accumulation.
For instance, Kural 385 says: "To acquire wealth, store it up, guard it, and distribute it wisely—these are the four distinct marks of an accomplished ruler (government)."

In practical terms, this means our leaders must stop treating national development projects as tools for cronyism or personal enrichment. Tax collected must be used for public benefit and every ringgit spent must be designed to uplift the people equitably.

The text places supreme importance on moral character and ethical duty. Leadership is not about bare political survival or relentless power plays; it is about steadfast integrity. As Kural 954 notes: “Even if wealth piled high is offered, those of good family will not do anything that lowers their honour.”
In a political culture scarred by broken promises, patronage politics, abuse of government resources and corruption, this is the missing link.

Ultimately, the Thirukkural is more than an ancient classic; it is a reality check for modern Malaysia. It reminds us that a nation’s true wealth is measured not by towering skyscrapers or quarterly GDP figures, but by the safety and dignity of its humblest citizen.
If our leaders have the courage to choose principled, people-centred governance over tactical survival, they - and we citizens - will find that Malaysia’s greatest days are still ahead.
